english: Allah!" "Did you really recognize him?" they asked. He answered: "Yes, and my heart is burning with enmity towards him"[Ibn Hisham 1/518, 519] An interesting story that took place on the first day, the Prophet ﷺ stepped in Madinah, could be quoted to illustrate the mental disturbance and deep anxiety that beset the Jews. ‘Abdullah bin Salam, the most learned rabbi among the Jews came to see the Prophet ﷺ when he arrived, and asked him certain questions to ascertain his real Prophethood.
kashmiri: اللہ!" تمو کوٚر پوٚچھمُت۔ "کیا تمو چُھ سُہٕ واقعی پَتہٕ زانان؟" تمو ونان۔ تمو ووٚن زِ "ہٕ، تہٕ مُہ سند دل چُہ تمس سۭتۍ دشمنی سۭتۍ برٛۄنٛہٕ وَنان۔" ابن ہشام 1/518, 519] اکھ دلچسپ کہانی یس گوڈنٕک روزہٕ پیٚٹھِ، نبی صلى الله عليه وسلم مدینہس منٛز قدم وٲل، یمن منٛز یمن یہودیو سٕتۍ ذہنی انتشار تہٕ گہری پریشانی ہاونہٕچ وضاحت کرنہٕ خٲطرٕ نقل کرنہٕ یوان۔  عبداللہ بن سلام، یہودیو منٛز سار

english: No sooner did he hear the Prophet’s answers than he embraced Islam, but added that if his people knew of his Islamization they would advance false arguments against me. The Prophet ﷺ sent for some Jews and asked them about ‘Abdullah bin Salam, they testified to his scholarly aptitude and virtuous standing. Here it was divulged to them that he had embraced Islam and on the spot, they imparted categorically opposite testimonies and described him as the most evil of all evils. In another narration ‘Abdullah bin Salam said, "O Jews! Be Allah fearing.
kashmiri: ییلہٕ سُہٕ پیغمبرن ہند جوابہٕ سنہٕ تہٕ تیم اسلام قبول کورمُت، مگر تیم زِ اگر تیم سٕند قوم سٕنٛد اسلام بندی ہند علم اوس گژھِتھ توہہِ سٕتۍ، توہہٕ سٕیۍ ونان زِ تیم سُندِس خلاف جھوٹے دلیلہٕ پیش کرِتھ۔ پیغمبرن کوٚر کچھ یہودیو پَتہٕ پَتٲر تہٕ سَمَس سٕنٛدی سٕنزِ "عبد اللہ بن سلام" سٕنٛزِ کتھہٕ، تمن کوٚرن سُنٛد علم تہٕ صالح مقامٕچ گواہی۔ اتھ منز آی سُو پتہٕ ز

english: By Allah, the only One, you know that he is the Messenger of Allah sent to people with the Truth." They replied, "You are lying." ... That was the Prophet’s first experience with the Jews.[Bukhari 1/459] That was the demo- political picture within Madinah. Five hundred kilometres away in Makkah, there still lay another source of detrimental threat, the archenemy of Islam, Quraish. For ten years, while at the mercy of Quraish, the Muslims were subjected to all sorts of terrorism, boycott, harassment and starvation coupled by a large scale painstaking psychological war and aggressive organized propaganda.
kashmiri: خدا سٕند قسم، صرف اکھ، تم چِھ زانان زِ تم چُھ خدا سُند رسول یم حقس سۭتۍ لوکن ہینز طرفہٕ آوُند بھیجا۔" تمن کوٚر جواب زِ" تم چَھ جھوٹ بولان۔" ... یہٕ اوس نبی سٕنز یہودیو سۭتۍ گوڑنک تجربہ۔ [بخاری 1/459] یہٕ ٲس مدینہ اندر ڈیمو-سیٲسی تصویر۔ پانچ سو کلومیٹر دور مکہس منز، اوس تہٕ نقصان دہ خطرٕک بیاکھ ذریعہٕ، اسلامک آرچ دشمن، قریش۔ دس وٕرین تام، قریش کہِ رحمٰن پیٹھ، مسلمانن ٲس ہر قسمک دہشت گرد

english: When they had emigrated to Madinah, their land, wealth and property were seized, wives detained and the socially humble in rank brutally tortured. Quraish also schemed and made attempts on the life of the first figure of the Call, Muhammad ﷺ . Due to their acknowledged temporal leadership and religious supremacy among the pagan Arabs, given the custodianship of the Sacred Sanctuary, the Quraishites spared no effort in enticing the Arabians against Madinah and boycotting the Madinese socially and economically. To quote Muhammad Al- Ghazali: "A state of war virtually existed between the Makkan tyrants and the Muslims in their abode.
kashmiri: جب تہندین زمین، دولت تہٕ املاک مدینہس منز ہجرت کرنس پیٹھ، تمن ہنٛد زمین، مال تہٕ مال چھ ضبط کرنہٕ آمت، زنانن چھ حراستس منٛز تھٲومٕت تہٕ معاشرتی طور پٲنٹھ عاجز درجہٕ دار چھ brutally tortured۔ قریش تہٕ کٔر کالک گوڈنٕک شخص محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم کس زندگی پیٹھ سازش تہٕ کوشش۔ مشرک عربن منٛز تہند تسلیم شدہ عارضی قیادت تہٕ مذہبی برتری ہنٛد وجہ سۭتۍ، مقدس مقدس مقامک نگہبانہٕت ہنٛدس نظرس منٛز، قریشین کوٚر مدینہٕ خلاف عربن راغب کرنہٕ تہٕ مدینہینینس معاشر

english: It is foolish to blame the Muslims for the horrible consequences that were bound to ensue in the light of that long- standing feud."[Fiqh As-Seerah p.162] The Muslims in Madinah were completely eligible then to confiscate the wealth of those tyrants, mete out for them exemplary punishment and bring twofold retaliation on them in order to deter them from committing any folly against the Muslims and their sanctities. That was a resume of the major problems that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ had to face, and the complicated issues he was supposed to resolve.
kashmiri: یہٕ چُھ بیہنس تام مسلمانن پیٹھ وٲلۍ تہٕ یمن ہیرودارۍ نتٲئجن خٲطرٕہ الزام لگان یُس اتھ طویل مدتی جھگڑس ہینز روشنی منٛز پٔدٕ گژھن واجن اوس۔"۔"""فیقه اس سیرا صفحہ 162] مدینہ منٛز مسلمان ٲسۍ یمن ظالمن ہنٛز دولت ضبط کرنہٕ، یمن خٲطرٕ نمونہٕ دار سزإچ تجویز کرنہٕ تہٕ مسلمانن تہٕ تمن ہنٛدس مقدساتس خلاف بیہٕ بیہِ بیہُن انتقامہٕ لگان تاکہ تمن مسلمانن سۭتۍ بیہس بیہچمتہٕ کرنہٕ خٲطرٕ۔ یہٕ ٲسۍ بنیٲدی مسائلن

english: In full acknowledgment, we could safely say that he quite honestly shouldered the responsibilities of Messengership, and cleverly discharged the liabilities of both temporal and religious leadership in Madinah. He accorded to everyone his due portion whether of mercy or punishment, with the former usually seasoning the latter in the overall process of establishing Islam on firm grounds among its faithful adherents.
kashmiri: پورٕ اعترافس منٛز، ہم ہیکن محفوظ طورس پیٹھ یہٕ کہہتھ زِ تیمو کوٚر منصفانہٕ طور پٲنٹھ رسولن ہٕنٛدۍ ذمہ داریاں قبول، تہٕ تمو کوٚرن مدینہ منٛز دنیٲی تہٕ مذہبی قیادتک ذمہ داریہٕ ذہین طور پٲٹھۍ پورا۔ تمو کٔر ہر اکس پننہٕ پورٕ حصہٕ یا رحم یا سزا ہنٛد، تیلہٕ گوڑن عام طورس پیٹھ اسلامس پننہِ وفادار پیروکارن درمیان مضبوط بنیادس پیٹھ قائم کرنہٕ کس مجموعی عملس منٛز امک ساروی کھوتہٕ زیادٕ ذائقہٕ۔

english: A New Society being built We have already mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ arrived in Madinah on Friday, 12th Rabi‘ Al- Awwal 1 A.H., i.e. September 27th. 622 A.D. and took the downstairs of Abi Ayyub’s house as a temporary residence. The first task to which the Prophetﷺ attended on his arrival in Madinah was the construction of a Mosque, in the very site where his camel knelt down. The land, which belonged to two orphans, was purchased.
kashmiri: اکھ نٔو معاشرٕ بناون وٲل۔ ہم چِھ گوڑنک ذکر کرمژ زِ رسول اللہ صلى الله عليه وسلم آو جمعہٕ، 12th ربیع الاول 1 ہِچ، یعنی 27th ستمبر 622 AD منز مدینہ تام تہٕ امہٕ کوٚر ابی ایوب کہِ گھرٕچ downstairs منزلہٕ عارضی رہائش گاہ۔ نبی صلى الله علیه وسلم مدینہس تام آمدس پیٹھ گوڑنچ کٲم یس تمس منز اوس شرکت کرمژ اوس تمس سائٹس پیٹھ ہیکہِ مسجدُک تعمیر، ییتھ پیٹھ تیم سٕندِ اونٹہٕ زانو۔ زمین، یوس زٕ یتیم لوکن ہند ٲس، اوس خرٔی آم

english: The Prophet ﷺ himself contributed to building the Mosque by carrying adobe bricks and stones while reciting verses: "O Allah! no bliss is there but that of the Hereafter, I beseech you to forgive the Emigrants and Helpers." The ground was cleared, of weeds and shrubs, palm trees and rubbish, the graves of the polytheists dug up and then levelled and the trees planted around. The Qiblah (the direction in which the Muslims turn their faces in prayer) was constructed to face Jerusalem; two beams were also erected to hold the ceiling up.
kashmiri: رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم سُوٛ ہیو مسجدٕ تعمیرس منٛز کٲم کٔرمٕژ تہٕ کٲشُر چِھ کٔشُری ہندِس کُن تہٕ پتھرس پیٹھ تہٕ آیتہٕ پڑھان: "اے اللہ، تہندِس بارس منٛز چُھ نہٕ تہٕ بیاکھ زندگی، مَیں چھہِ تمس پیٹھ پَتہٕ آمُت زِ تم ہجرت کرن وٲل تہٕ مدد کرن وأل۔" زمینچ صفائی آی کرنہٕ، جھاڑ تہٕ جھاڑیو، کھجور تہٕ کچہٕ، مشرکین ہنٛز قبریں کھینٛڑٲو تہٕ پتہٕ س

english: It was square in form, each side measuring approximately 100 yards, facing towards the north and having three gates on each of the remaining sides. Nearby, rooms reserved for the Prophet’s household were built of stones and adobe bricks with ceilings of palm leaves. [Bukhari 1/71,555,560; Za'd Al- Ma'ad 2/56] To the north of the Mosque a place was reserved for the Muslims who had neither family nor home. The Adhân (summoning the Muslims to the Mosque by the Call for prayer) was initiated at this early stage of post- migration era.
kashmiri: یہٕ اوس مربع شکلہٕ، ہر طرف تقریباً 100 گز پیمائش، شمالس طرف آمت تہٕ باقیہٕ طرفن منٛز چِھ ترٛیٛن دروازن ہنز۔ قریب، پیغمبروں ہٕنٛدس گھرس خٲطرٕ مخصوص کمرن ٲس پتھروں تہٕ اڈوب برکن سۭتۍ تعمیر آمت کرنہٕ یمن منٛز کھجورٕ ہٕنٛز پتیہٕ چِھ۔ [بخاری 1/71,555,560؛ زعید المعاد 2/56] مسجدٕچ شمالس منٛز اوس مسلمانن خٲطرٕہ اکھ جایہ مخصوص آمت یم نہٕ کنبہٕ تہٕ نہٕ گھر ٲس۔ مسجدٕ (دعوت نمازٕ خٲطرٕ مسلمن مسجدس

english: The Mosque was not merely a locus to perform prayers, but rather an Islamic league where the Muslim’s were instructed in Islam and its doctrines. It served as an assembly place where the conflicting pre- Islamic trends used to come to terms; it was the headquarter wherein all the affairs of the Muslims were administered, and consultative and executive councils held. The Mosque being thus constructed, the Prophet ﷺ next turned his attention to cementing the ties of mutual brotherhood amongst the Muslims of Madinah, Al- Ansar (the Helpers) and Al- Muhajirun (the Emigrants). It was indeed unique in the history of the world.
kashmiri: مسجد اوس نہٕ صرف نماز ادا کرنٕچ جایہٕ بلکہ اکھ اسلامی لیگ ییتھ منٛز مسلمانن اسلام تہٕ امچ نظریاتس منٛز تعلیم دیوان۔ یہٕ بنیو اکھ اجتماعچ جایٕ ییتہٕ متضاد قبل از اسلامی رجحانات ٲس آمت۔ یہ اوس ہیڈکوارٹر ییتس منٛز مسلمانو ہنٛد تمام معاملات چِھ زیر انتظام، تہٕ مشورتی تہٕ ایگزیکٹو کونسلہٕ چِھ۔ مسجد اوس یتھ پٲٹھۍ بناونہٕ آمت، نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن کوٚر پتہٕ پنن توجہ مدینہٕ کس مسلمانن، الانسار (محمدین) تہٕ الہاجیرون (مغٲرمن) درمیان با

english: A gathering of 90 men, half of whom Emigrants and the others Helpers assembled in the house of Anas bin Malik where the Prophet ﷺ gave the spirit of brotherhood his official blessing. When either of the two persons who had been paired as brothers, passed away, his property was inherited by his brother- in- faith.
kashmiri: 90 لوکن ہند اکھ اجتماع، یمن منٛز نصف ایمگرین تہٕ باقی ہیلپرز انس بن مالک کہِ گھرس منز جمع گژھنہٕ آمت، یتہِ نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن بھائیچارن ہند روحس پننہِ سرکٲری برکت دیُت۔ ییلہِ زٕ شخصن منٛز اکھ یم بھائِن پانٹھ جوڑنہٕ آمُت ٲس، مرن، تیم سٕنز جائیدادٕ سُند بھائس- ایمانس سٕتۍ ورثہٕ۔

english: This practice continued till the following verse was revealed at the time of the battle of Badr, and the regular rule of inheritance was allowed to take its usual course: "But kindred by blood are nearer to one another regarding inheritance [Za'd Al- Ma'ad 2/56]." [Al- Qur'an 8:75] "Brotherhood- in- faith" to quote Muhammad Al- Ghazali again, "was holding subordinate every distinction of race and kindred and supporting the Islamic precept: none is superior to the other except on the basis of piety and God- fearing. [Fiqh AsSeerah p140,141]"
kashmiri: یہٕ عمل گوو تمس تام جاری یوتتھ تام زِ بدر کہ جنگ کس وقتہٕ آو یمہِ آیتہٕ نازل کرنہٕ، تہٕ ورثہٕ ہنٛد باقاعدہ اصولس اوس پننہٕ معمولک طریقہٕ اختیار کرنہٕ آمت: "مگر خونہٕ سۭتۍ تعلق تھاوان چِھ ورثس متعلق اکھ بییہٕ قریب [زعد المعاد 2/56]۔" [القرآن 8:75] "خاندانس منٛز ایمان" محمد الغزالی دوبارٕ نقل کرنہٕ خٲطرٕ، "رٕجٲنی تہٕ رشتہٕ کہِ ہر فرقس تابع تھاوان اوس تہٕ اسلامی اصولچ تائید کران: اکھ چُھ نہٕ بییہِ پیٹھہ

english: The Prophet ﷺ attached to that brotherhood a valid contract; it was not just meaningless words but rather a valid practice relating to blood and wealth rather than a passing whim taking the form of accidental greeting. The atmosphere of brotherhood and fellow- feeling created a spirit of selflessness infused deeply in the hearts of his followers, and produced very healthy results. For example, Sa‘d bin Ar- Rabi‘, a Helper, said to his fellow brother ‘Abdur Rahman bin ‘Awf, "I am the richest man amongst the Helpers. I am glad to share my property half and half with you.
kashmiri: نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن کوٚر اتھ برادریس اکھ معتبر معاہدٕ۔ یہ ٲس نہ صرف بے معنی الفاظ بلکہ خون تہٕ دولتس سۭتۍ متعلق اکھ معتبر عمل بلکہ حادثاتی سلامچ شکلہٕ تھون وٲل ایکہٕ گزری وٲلی مٲہر۔ برادری تہٕ ہمدردی ہنٛد ماحولن کوٚرمت پننہٕ پیروکارن ہنٛز دلین منٛز گہری بے جانی ہنٛدس جذبس منٛز اضافہ، تہٕ یہٕ کٔر واریاہ صحی نتائج۔ مثال کہِ طورس پیٹھ، سعد بن آر ربی، اکھ مددگار، پننہِ ساتھی بھائی ابدر رحمان بن اوفس سٕتۍ کوٚر یہٕ کہ "مَنٛہٕ چھِ

english: I have two wives, I am ready to divorce one and after the expiry of her ‘Iddah, (the prescribed period for a woman divorcee to stay within her house unmarried) you may marry her." But ‘Abdur Rahman bin ‘Awf was not prepared to accept anything: neither property nor home. So he blessed his brother and said: "Kindly direct me to the market so that I may make my fortune with my own hands." And he did prosper and got married very shortly by his own labour. [Bukhari 1/553]
kashmiri: مےٚ چھ زٕ زنانہٕ، تِہندِس أکس طلاقہِ خأطرِ چُھ زِ تیمہِ سٕندِ طلاقہٕ پتہٕ ہیکو زنہٕ۔" مگر عبدالرحمن بن عارف کرنس پننہِ مالہٕ تہٕ پننہٕ مکانس منز کانٛہہ تہٕ حٲصل کرنس نہٕ تیار۔ امہِ پأٹھۍ سُہ پننین بھائِس پیٹھ برکت وٲلۍ تہٕ وُلۍ سَرٲو پننِس مرضی پَتہٕ مَنٛدی پنن پانہٕ وٲتِتھ۔ تہٕ سُوٛ گو پنن وٲنۍ محنت

english: The Helpers were extremely generous to their brethren- in- faith. Abu Hurairah reported that they once approached the Prophet ﷺ with the request that their orchards of palm trees should be distributed equally between the Muslims of Madinah and their brethren from Makkah. But the Prophet ﷺ was reluctant to put this heavy burden upon them. It was, however, decided that the Emigrants would work in the orchards alongwith the Helpers and the yield would be divided equally amongst them.
kashmiri: امہٕ وقتہٕ، امہِ وقتہِ اوس امہُک اکھ اہم کردار ادا کرنہٕ آمت۔ امہَس دوران اوس امس سٕتۍ ملنہٕ آمُت امہنز برادران۔ ابو ہریرہن گو زِ تمو کوٚر اکھ بار نبی صلى الله عليه وسلم سٕنز منتظری زِ یمن ہنٛد کھجورٕ ہٕنٛدۍ باغہٕ تہٕ یمن ہنٛد مکہٕ ہِنٛدۍ برادرانن درمیان برابر تقسیم کرنہٕ۔ مگر نبی صلى اللہ عليه وسلم اوس یمن پیٹھ یہٕ بھاری بوجھ تھونہٕ خٲطرٕ ہچکچاہٹ۔ تاہم، یہٕ گو فیصلہ زِ تارکین وطنن گژھِ امہس سٔتۍ کھجورِ ہ

english: [Bukhari 1/312] Such examples point directly to the spirit of sacrifice, altruism and cordiality on the part of the Helpers, and also to the feeling of appreciation, gratitude and self- respect that the Emigrants held dear to their hearts. They took only what helped them eke a reasonable living. In short, this policy of mutual brotherhood was so wise and timely that many obstinate problems were resolved wonderfully and reasonably.
kashmiri: [بخاری 1/312] یتھ مثالن منٛز چھ امہٕ قسمک مظاہرین ہنٛد جانبٕ قربانی، ہمدردی تہٕ دلکش جذباتس براہ راست اشارہ کران، تہٕ امہِ سۭتۍ سۭتۍ امہُک تعریف، شکر گزار تہٕ خود اعتمادی ہنٛد احساسس پیٹھ تہٕ یم امہین ہجرت کرن وٲلین ہنٛد دلن منٛز ساروی کھوتہٕ زیٛادٕ تھاوان۔ تمو صرف یہٕ چُھ لےومُت یُس یمن سٕتۍ معقول زندگی گزارن منٛز مدد کٔر۔ مختصر طور پٲنٹھ، باہمی برادری ہنٛز یہٕ پالیسی ٲس تییہٕ دانشمند تہٕ بروقت کہ واریاہ سخت مسائل ٲس حیرت انگیز تہٕ مع

english: A Charter of Islamic Alliance Just as the Prophet ﷺ had established a code of brotherhood amongst the believers, so too he was keen on establishing friendly relations between the Muslims and non- Muslim tribes of Arabia. He established a sort of treaty aiming at ruling out all pre- Islamic rancour and inter- tribal feuds. He was so meticulous not to leave any area in the charter that would allow pre- Islamic traditions to sneak in or violate the new environment he wanted to establish. Herein, we look over some of its provisions. In the Name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful.
kashmiri: اسلامک اتحادُک ایکہِ چارٹر یتھ پٲٹھۍ نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن مسلمانن درمیان اخوتک ایکِس کوڈچ تعٲمیر کٔرِتھ، تمو کوٚر عربی عربس منز مسلمانن تہٕ غأر مسلم قبیلن درمیان دوستانہ تعلقات قائم کرنُک شوق۔ تمو کٔرمٕژ اکھ قسمُک معاہدہ یُس پَتہٕ اسلامس برونٹھ کین کینٛہہ کینٛہہ تہٕ نسلی اختلافن ہینز تردید کرنُچ چِھ مقصد۔ تم ٲسِس اتہٕ پَتٔ پَٹھ محتاط زِ تمو نہٕ چارٹرس منٛز کُنہٕ تہ علاقہٕ نچھان زِ یہٕ چ

english: This is a document from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, concerning Emigrants and Helpers and those who followed and strove with them.
kashmiri: یہِ چُھ پیغمبرن ہند اکھ کتاب یُس پیٹھہ چُھ۔ (یہ کتاب) تارکین وطن تہٕ امہِ سرکشین پیٹھہٕ تہِ یمن سۭتۍ بہٕ کٲم کرن وٲلۍ تہِ جنگ کرن وولن وول۔

english: 1. They are one nation to the exclusion of other people. 2. The Emigrants of Quraish unite together and shall pay blood money among themselves, and shall ransom honourably their prisoners. Every tribe of the Helpers unite together, as they were at first, and every section among them will pay a ransom for acquitting its relative prisoners. 3. Believers shall not leave anyone destitute among them by not paying his redemption money or blood money in kind.
kashmiri: 1. تم چِھ بیاکھ قوم۔ 2. قریش سٕندِ ہجرت کرن وٲلۍ لوک چِہ اکھ ملنہٕ تہٕ پننِس درمیان خونہٕ ہنز پیمائش کرِتھ تہٕ پَتہٕ پٔدٕ گژھن وٲلس قَسَمَن ہنز فدیہٕ۔ امہِ کِس قبیلہِ سٕنز مدد کرن وَنِو پَتٔ چِھ۔ تہٕ تمن منز چِه ہر ایکہِ پنن قَسمہِ قَکَن ہند فدیھ دِوان۔

english: 4. Whoever is rebellious or whoever seeks to spread enmity and sedition, the hand of every God- fearing Muslim shall be against him, even if he be his son.
kashmiri: 4. یُس بغاوتک مرتکب گژھہِ یا دشمنی تہِ بغاوت پھیلاونہٕچ کوشش کرِتھ، تہٕ یُتھ زَن تہٕ تہندِ اولاد آسہٕ، تہندٕ خَدایس نِش پرٛیٚتھ مسلمانن ہنزِ دٲخِل آسہِ تیمس خلاف

english: 5. A believer shall not kill another believer, nor shall support a disbeliever against a believer. 6. The protection of Allah is one (and is equally) extended to the humblest of the believers. 7. The believers are supported by each other. 8. Whosoever of the Jews follows us shall have aid and succour; they shall not be injured, nor any enemy be aided against them. 9. The peace of the believers is indivisible. No separate peace shall be made when believers are fighting in the way of Allah. Conditions must be fair and equitable to all. 10.
kashmiri: مُتلق چُھنہٕ مسلمانن ہنز جان تُلان، تہٕ نہٕ کافر چُھ مسلمان کس خلاف مدد کران، تہندین اولادن ہنٛدس بارس منٛز چُہ نہٕ کرُن کانٛہہ تہٕ نمائندگی۔ یُس یُہودِیَن پیٹھ چُھ آمُت، تَس چُھنٔ کانہ تِہ کانہ نقصان گژھان۔ تَتھ پیٹھ چِھ نہٕ کانہ خۄداےَس دُشمن پیٹھ کانہ نٔ کانہہ تہِ مدد آسِ۔ حالاتن ہٕنٛدۍ چھِ پورٕن خٲطرٕہ منصفانہٕ تہٕ منصفان۔

english: It shall not be lawful for a believer, who holds by what is in this document and believes in Allah and the Day of Judgement, to help a criminal nor give him refuge. Those who give him refuge and render him help shall have the curse and anger of Allah on the Day of Resurrection. Their indemnity is not accepted. 11. Whenever you differ about a matter, it must be referred to Allah and to Muhammad.[Ibn Hisham 1/502,503] 12. Killing a believer deliberately with no good reason entails killing the killer unless the sponsor deems it otherwise.
kashmiri: یُس مؤمن چُھ یُتھ پیٹھ یقین تھاوان زِ کتابِ منز چُھنہٕ یُن کتھہٕ تھاوان تہٕ خداس تہٕ قیامتس پیٹھ چُہ نہٕ ایمان تھاوان کہ تمن چُھ۔ یِم تہٕ یِمن یمن پیٹھ یقین آسہٕ آسہِ تہندین پیٹھ چِھ خداک لعنت تہٕ غضب قیامتس منٛز آسان۔ تمن ہنٛد بدلہٕ چُنہٕ قبول کرنہٕ آمُت۔

english: It was solely by his wisdom and dexterity, that the Prophet ﷺ erected the pillars of the new society. This phenomenon no doubt left its mark on the virtuous Muslims. He used to bring them up in the light of the Islamic education, he sanctified their selves, enjoined them to observe righteousness and praiseworthy manners and was keen on infusing into them the ethics of amity, glory, honour, worship and first and foremost obedience to Allah and His Messenger.
kashmiri: صرف پننہِ حکمت تہٕ ہنر ہیوندِ ذریعہِ ہیکو نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن نٔو معاشرس ہند ستون کھینچُن۔ یہٕ مظاہرٕ کٔر بلاشبہ صالح مسلمانن پیٹھ پننہٕ نشان۔ تمن اوس اسلامک تعلیم کہِ روشنی منز روزان، تمن پننِس مقدس بناوان، تمو سٕتۍ امہِ عملن ہند مشاہدٕ کران تہٕ تمن ٲسِس دوستی، جلال، عزت، عبادت تہٕ اول تہٕ اہم طورس پیٹھ اللہ تہٕ تیم سٕندِس رسولس مطٲعیتُک اخلاقیات انڈول کرنس منز پرزٲن۔

english: The following is a cluster of the virtues he used to inculcate in the minds of his followers: A man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which of the merits is superior in Islam. He (the Prophet ﷺ) remarked: "That you provide food and extend greetings to one whom you know or do not know."[Bukhari 1/6,9] ‘Abdullah bin Salâm said: When the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah, I went to see him and I immediately recognized through his features that he would never be a liar.
kashmiri: یہٕ چُھ پننین پیروکارن ہینز ذہنن منٛز چھِ سُہٕ پننِس ذہنس منٛز چھُ وٲل کرنچ عادت۔ اکھ مردن کوٚر رسول اللہ صلى الله عليه وسلمس پُنٛس یُس اسلامس منٛز کس ذہنیتس منز چُھ۔ تمن (نبی صلى الله علیه وسلم) کوٚر یہٕ ذکر: "یہٕ کہ تم چھِ تمن تام خوراک فراہم کران تہٕ تمن سۭتۍ سلام چھِ کران یس تمن چُھنہٕ زانان یا نہٕ زانٛہہ۔" [بخاری 1/6,9]  عبداللہ بن سلامن کوٚرن:

english: The first things he (the Prophet ﷺ) said was: "Extend peace greetings amongst yourselves, provide food to the needy, maintain uterine relations, observe prayer at night while people are asleep, then you will peacefully enter the Garden (Paradise)."[Narrated by At-Tirmidhi; Mishkat AlMasabih 1/168]
kashmiri: تمن گوڑنک چیزو اوس تم (نبی صلى الله عليه وسلم) ووٚن: "تمہٕ درمیان امن سلامات پھیلاؤ، ضرورت مندن ہینز خوراک فراہم کرو، رحم ہنٛد رشتہٕ برقرار رکھو، راتس نماز ادا کرو ییلہٕ لوکھ نیندٕ چھ، تہٕ تم ہیکو جنتس (جنت) منٛز امن سان داخل گژھتھ۔"

english: And he said:
kashmiri: تہٕ سُوٛ وُچھتھ:

english: "The Muslim is that one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe.[Bukhari 1/6]" And said: "None amongst you believes (truly) till one likes for his brother that which he loves for himself.[ibid 1/6]" And said: "He will not enter Paradise, he whose neighbour is not secure from his wrongful conduct.[Narrated by Muslim; Mishkat Al- Masabih 2/422]" And said: "A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim; he neither oppresses him nor does he fail him. Whosoever removes a worldly grief from a believer, Allah will remove from him one of the griefs of the Day of Judgement.
kashmiri: مسلمان چُھ تمن سٕندِس زبانہٕ تہٕ ہاتھس پیٹھ یقین آسہٕ آمُت۔ تہٕ تمن منٛز چُھنہٕ کانٛہہ تہٕ مؤمن یوتتھ تام زِ تمن ہنٛدس بھائس پیٹھ چُھ۔ یُس پننہٕ خأطرٕ چُہ پسند کران چُھو، تہٕ چِھ نہٕ جنتس منٛز پَننِس ہمسایہٕ سٕنٛدس ظلمس پیٹھ امن آسہِ۔

english: Whosoever shields a Muslim, Allah will shield him on the Day of Resurrection.[Mishkat AlMasabih 2/422; Sahih Al- Bukhari; Sahih Muslim]" And said: "Abusing a Muslim is an outrage and fighting against him is disbelief.[Bukhari 2/893]" And said: "To remove something harmful from the road, is charity.[Mishkat Al- Masabih 1/12]" And said: "Charity erases sins just as water extinguishes fire.[ibid 1/14]" And said: "He is not a perfect believer, who goes to bed full and knows that his neighbour is hungry.[ibid 2/424]" And said: "Show mercy to people on earth so that Allah will have mercy on you in heaven.[Sunan Abu Da'ud 2/235]" And said: "Try to avert fire even by half a date (in charity) if not by tendering a good word.
kashmiri: یُس مسلمانس پیٹھ ڈھالہٕ تہٕ روزن چُھ، خدا چُہ قیامتس پیٹھ تہٕ دِتھ۔ [مشکت المسابیح 2/422؛ صحیح البخاری، صحیحیح مسلم] تہٕ وُوچھِتھ، "مسلمس پیٹھ حملہٕ کرنا چُھ۔ یہٕ چُھنہٕ زیادٕہ زیادٕ بدسلوکی۔ تہٕ تمس خلاف لڑنا چُھو کفر۔ [محمد بخاری 2/893]" تہٕ "سڑک پیٹھہٕ نقصان دہ چیز ہٹانا چُو صدقات۔ [مسکت المسیح 1/12]" تہِ وُچھِت، "صحیحیت چُس

english: [Bukhari 2/190]" And said:
kashmiri: [بوخاری 2/190]" تہٕ وُچھُن:

english: "Clothing an under- clad Muslim, entitles you to a garment from the Paradise; feeding a hungry Muslim will make you eligible (by Allah’s Will) for the fruit of the Paradise, and if you provide water to a thirsty Muslim, Allah will provide you with a drink from ‘the Sealed Nectar’.[Mishkat Al- Masabih 1/169]" He used as well to exhort the believers to spend in charity reminding them of relevant virtues for which the hearts yearn.
kashmiri: تمن ہنٛدس بارس منٛز چُھ تمن ہنٛز کٲمِچ ضرورت آسان۔ تمن چُھنہٕ یمن ہنٛدس وقتس منٛز روزان۔ تم چِھ یمن ہنٛد پانس خۄدمۄختار بناوان۔ تم چھِ یمن ہنٛد استعمال کران، تم چُہ یمن ہنٛد کھاتہٕ کھینچِتھ، تمن چھِ جنتک لباس پہننہٕ، تم چھُ یمن ہنٛدن کھاتس کھیننہٕ خٲطرٕہ تمن خۄد آسہِ اہل۔ تم ہیکن یمن ہنٛدین کھاتن پیٹھ چُھ۔ تمن منٛز چِھ۔ تم چَھ یمن ہنٛز کھاتھ کھینچی چِھنہِ، تم ہیکو جنتک کٲش

english: He said: "The believers in their mutual love, are like the human body where when the eye is in agony, the entire body feels the pain; when the head aches, all the body will suffer. [Narrated by Muslim]" And said: "The bonds of brotherhood between two Muslims are like parts of a house, one part strengthens and holds the other.[Bukhari 2/890]" And said: "Do not have malice against a Muslim; do not be envious of other Muslims; do not go against a Muslim and forsake him. O the slaves of Allah! Be like brothers with each other.
kashmiri: تمو کوٚر یہٕ دلیل زِ مسلمانن درمیان بھائری ہند تعلق چُھ اکھ مکانک حصن ہینزِ مانند۔ اکھ حصہٕ چُہ مضبوط کران تہٕ بیاکھ چُھ۔ (بخاری 2/890) تہٕ تمو چُھنہٕ مسلمانن پیٹھ کُنہٕ بدچلن وٲل۔ تمن پیٹھ چُھو نہٕ کُن حسد وٲلن، تمن چُن نہٕ مسلمانس پیٹھ چِھ حملہٕ کران تہ تم چِھنہِ اَسہِ پیٹھ دُور گژان۔ اے خدا کے بندو! تم چُو ایکِس بیاکہِس سٕتۍ بھائرن ہینٛد رشتہ

english: It is not violable for a Muslim to desert his brother for over three days.[Bukhari 2/896]" The Prophet ﷺ used as well to promote that habit of abstention from asking the others for help unless one is totally helpless. He used to talk to his companions a lot about the merits, virtues and Divine reward implied in observing the prescribed worships and rituals.
kashmiri: مسلمانن خٲطرٕ چھ نہٕ یہٕ خلاف ورزی زِ پننٛنہِ بھائِس ترٛیٚہ روزہٕ تام چھِ ترک کران۔ [بخاری 2/896] " نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن کوٚر یہٕ عادت تہٕ فروغ زِ اگر اکھ مکمل طور پٲنٹھ بے بس چھِ نہٕ، تیلہٕ چھِ باقیو سۭتۍ مدد طلب کرنہٕ نہٕ کرنہٕ۔ تم ٲس پننہِ ساتھین سۭتۍ مقررہ عبادت تہٕ رسوماتہٕ پَرٕزنہٕ سۭتۍ وابستہٕ گژھن وٲلۍ فضائل، فضائل تہٕ الہی انعامن متعلق واریاہ کتھ کران۔

english: He would always bring forth corroborated proofs in order to link them physically and spiritually to the Revelation sent to him, hence he would apprise them of their duties and responsibilities in terms of the consequences of the Call of Islam, and at the same time emphasize the exigencies of comprehension and contemplation. That was his practice of maximizing their morale and imbuing them with the noble values and ideals so that they could become models of virtue to be copied by subsequent generations.
kashmiri: سُہٕ اوس ہمیشہٕ جسمٲنی تہٕ روحانی طورس پیٹھ یمن پننین پاسہٕ آمت وحیس سۭتۍ جڑتھ ثأبت کرنہٕ خٲطرٕہ ثابت ثبوتہٕ نوان، تہٕ امہٕ وجہ سۭتۍ اوس سُهند علم اسلامک کال کہِ نتائجن ہندِ لحاظٕ سٕتۍ یمن ہنٛز ڈیوٹیزن تہٕ ذمہ دارین سۭتۍ، تہِ اتھ وقتس منز اوس سمجان تہٕ غور کرنٕچ ضرورتس پیٹھ زور دیوان۔ یہٕ اوس سٕندِس اخلاقیاتس بڑھانُک تہٕ پٔتھرین نسلن ہینز نقل کرنہٕ خاطرٕ تمن منز فضلیتُک نمونہٕ بننہٕ خٲطرِ یم انن منز شریف

english: ‘Abdullah bin Mas‘ud رضی اللہ عنہ once said: If you are willing to follow a good example, then you can have a recourse in the tradition of the deceased, because the living are likely to fall an easy victim to oppression (so they might waver in faith). Follow the steps of Muhammad’s Companions. They were the best in this nation, the most pious, the most learned and the least pretentious. Allah chose them to accompany the Prophet ﷺ and establish His religion.
kashmiri: عبداللہ بن مسعود رضی اللہ عنہما ونے کہو اگر تمن اوس اکھ نیک نمونہٕ پیروی کرنُک ارادہ تہٕ تم ہیکن مرن وول سنتس پیٹھ رجوع کرتھ، کیازکہ زندٕہ چِھ آسان زِ مظلومن پیٹھ چُھ آسان ظلم۔ تہٕ محمد (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) سٕندین صحابینن ہنز پَننِس پَنِس پیٹھ چِھو لٹان۔ یہٕ ٲسۍ امہِ امتک بہترین، پرہیزگار، علم وشن وول تہٕ کم ہیکن نہٕ بڑبڑ۔ اللہ نے تمن پیغمبرکس ہمراہ چُھنہٕ تہٕ پنن دین قائم کرنس

english: Therefore, it is imperative to get to know their grace, follow their righteous way and adhere as much as you can to their manners and assimilate their biography. They were always on the orthodox path. There is then the great Messenger of Allah ﷺ whose moral visible attributes, aspects of perfection, talents, virtues, noble manners and praiseworthy deeds, entitle him to occupy the innermost cells of our hearts, and become the dearest target that the self
kashmiri: لہذا، یہٕ چُھ ضروری زِ تمن ہنٛد فضل جاننہٕ، تمن ہنٛز صالح راہچ پیروی کرُن تہٕ تمن ہند طرز عملس پیٹھ یوتتھ تام تم ہیکن عمل کرُتھ تہٕ یمن ہنٛز سوانح عمری ہنز سمٲجی۔ تم ٲس ہمیشہٕ ترٲوِتھ ارتدوکس سڑکس پیٹھ۔ تہٕ تہٕ چِھ خداک عظیم رسول صلى الله عليه وسلم یُس اخلاقی طور پٲنٹھ نظر یوان آسہٕ، کمال، صلاحیتن، فضائلن، شریف طرز عملن تہِ قابلِ تعریف عملن ہند پہلوؤں، تمس چُہِ امس حق دِتھ کہ تمن ہینز دلک اندرونی خلی

english: yearns for. Hardly did he utter a word when his Companions would race to assimilate it and work in its light.[Mishkat Al-Masabih 1/32] Those were the attributes and qualities on whose basis the Prophet ﷺ wanted to build a new society, the most wonderful and the most honourable society ever known in history. On these grounds, he strove to resolve the longstanding problems, and later gave mankind the chance to breathe a sigh of relief after a long wearying journey in dark and gloomy avenues.
kashmiri: تمن ٲسۍ صفاتن تہٕ خصلتن پیٹھ مبنی یم پیٹھ نبی صلى الله عليه وسلم اکھ نٔو معاشرٕ بناونہٕ چاہت، تاریخس منٛز ساروی کھوتہٕ شاندار تہٕ ساروی ساروی پیٹھہٕ قابلِ احترام معاشرُک۔ یمن بنیادن پیٹھ، تمن کوٚر طویل مدتی مسائل حل کرنہٕ خٲطرٕ کوشش، تہٕ پتہٕ کوٚر انسانس اندھس تہٕ اندھمس منٛز طویل تھکن وٲل سفرہٕ پتہِ چھِ امہٕ سۭتۍ راحتک سانسہٕ ننہٕچ موقع۔

english: Such lofty morale lay at the very basis of creating a new society with integrated components immune to all fluctuations of time, and powerful enough to change the whole course of humanity.
kashmiri: یِتھٕ کٔنی بلند مورال اوس اکھ نٔو معاشرٕچ تشکیل ہنٛز بنیاد بنیومُت ییتھ منٛز مربوط اجزاء وقتک تمام اتار چڑھاؤن سۭتۍ محفوظ چِھ، تہٕ انسانیتک پورٕ رخ تبدیل کرنہٕ خٲطرٕہ کافی طاقتور چِھ۔

english: A Cooperation and Non-Aggression Pact with the Jews Soon after emigrating to Madinah and making sure that the pillars of the new Islamic community were well established on strong bases of administrative, political and ideological unity, the Prophet ﷺ commenced to establish regular and clearlydefined relations with non- Muslims. All of these efforts were exerted solely to provide peace, security, and prosperity to all mankind at large, and to bring about a spirit of rapport and harmony within his region, in particular. Geographically, the closest people to Madinah were the Jews.
kashmiri: یہودیو سۭتۍ تعاون تہٕ عدم جارحیتک معاہدٕ۔ مدینہ ہجرت کرنہٕ پتہٕ تہٕ یہٕ یقینی بناونہٕ کہ نوٕ اسلامی برادری ہنٛد ستون انتظامی، سیاسی تہٕ نظریٲتی اتحادک مضبوط بنیادس پیٹھ چِھ قائم، نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن کوٚر غٲر مسلمو سۭتۍ باقاعدہ تہٕ واضح تعلقات قائم۔ یہٕ تمام کوششہٕ ٲس صرف ساری انسانیتس امن، سلامتی تہٕ خوشحالی فراہم کرنہٕ خٲطرٕہ کرنہٕ آمت، تہٕ خاص طور پٲنٹھ پننہٕ خطس اندر رشتہٕ تہِ ہم آہنگی ہنٛز روحس پٔدٕ کرنہٕ خاطرٕ۔ جغرافیائی طورس پیٹھ، مدینہٕ سۭتۍ قریبی ترین لو

english: Whilst harbouring evil intentions, and nursing bitter grudge, they showed not the least resistance nor the slightest animosity. The Prophet decided to ratify a treaty with them with clauses that provided full freedom in faith and wealth. He had no intention whatsoever of following severe policies involving banishment, seizure of wealth and land or hostility. The treaty came within the context of another one of a larger framework relating to inter- Muslim relationships. The most important provisions of the treaty are the following:
kashmiri: ییلہٕ تہٕ تمن منٛز ٲس بد نیت تہٕ تلخ کینہہ تہٕ، تمن کوٚر نہٕ کم کھوتہٕ کم مزاحمت تہٕ نہٕ معمولی دشمنی۔ نبین کوٚرمت یہٕ فیصلہ زِ تمن سۭتۍ اکھ معاہدٕ چُھ اتھ شقہٕ سۭتۍ دستخط کرنہٕ یُس ایمان تہٕ دولتس منٛز مکمل آزادی فراہم کران۔ تمن اوس نہٕ کنہہ تہِ ارادہ زِ ملک بدر، دولت تہٕ زمین یا دشمنس سۭتۍ متعلق سخت پالیسیہٕ پیروی کرنہٕ۔ یہٕ معاہدہٕ بنیو بین مسلم تعلقاتن متعلق اکھ بیاکھ بڑ فریم ورکس سیاقس منٛز۔ معاہدس منٛز ساروی کھوتہِ اہم شق

english: 1. The Jews of Bani ‘Awf are one community with the believers. The Jews will profess their religion, and the Muslims theirs. 2. The Jews shall be responsible for their expenditure, and the Muslims for theirs. 3. If attacked by a third party, each shall come to the assistance of the other. 4. Each party shall hold counsel with the other. Mutual relation shall be founded on righteousness; sin is totally excluded. 5. Neither shall commit sins to the prejudice of the other. 6. The wronged party shall be aided. 7.
kashmiri: 1. بنی آوفک یہودی چِھ مؤمنن سٕتۍ اکھ برادری۔ یہودی چُھ پننِس مذہبُک اقرار کران، تہٕ مسلمان چِھ۔ 2. یہودی چَھ پننہِ اخراجاتُک ذمہ دار، تہ مسلمان چُھ۔ 3. اگر ترٛیٚیمہٕ شخصٕ پیٹھ حملہٕ کرنہٕ تہٕ ہر ایکِس بییہٕ طرفہٕ مدد کرنہٕ۔ 4. ہر ایکہِ طرفہِ سٕندِس ساتھ مشورٕ کرُن۔ باہمی تعلقات چِہِ صداقتس پیٹھ مبنی آسان۔ گناہ چُھنہٕ پورٕ طورس پیٹھ خارج۔ 5. نہٕ بییہِ طرفس خلاف گناہ کٔرِتھ۔ 6. مظلوم

english: The Jews shall contribute to the cost of war so long as they are fighting alongside the believers. 8. Madinah shall remain sacred and inviolable for all that join this treaty. 9. Should any disagreement arise between the signatories to this treaty, then Allah, the All- High and His Messenger shall settle the dispute. 10. The signatories to this treaty shall boycott Quraish commercially; they shall also abstain from extending any support to them. 11. Each shall contribute to defending Madinah, in case of a foreign attack, in its respective area. 12. This treaty shall not hinder either party from seeking lawful revenge.[Ibn Hisham 1/503,504]
kashmiri: یُہودین گژھہِ جنگہٕ کہِ اخراجاتس منز حصہٕ ننہٕ یوتتھ تام زِ تمن چِھ مؤمنن سٕتۍ جنگ کران۔ 8۔ مدینہ چُھ اتھ معاہدس منٛز شمولیت اختیار کرن وٲل تمام افرادن خٲطرٕ مقدس تہٕ ناقابلِ رساو۔ 9۔ اگر اتھ معاہدےس منٛز دستخط کرن وٕنین درمیان کُنہٕ اختلاف آسہٕ، تہٕ خدا، بلند ترین تہٕ سُند رسول چُہ اتھ اختلافس حل کران۔ 10۔ اتھ معاہدنس منٛز signatoriesن چُھ۔ یہٕ معاہدٕ کرن وۄنۍ قریشس تجارتی طور پیٹھ بائیکاٹ۔ تہٕ تمن آو

english: Madinah and its suburbs, after the ratification of this treaty, turned into a coalition state, with Madinah proper as capital and Muhammad ﷺ as ‘president’; authorities lay mainly in the hand of the Muslims, and consequently it was a real capital of Islam. To expand the zone of peace and security the Prophet ﷺ started to enter into similar treaties with other tribes living around ‘his state’.
kashmiri: مدینہ تہٕ امچ مضافات، اتھ معاہدس ہنٛز تائید پتہٕ، اکھ اتحاد ریاست منٛز تبدیل گٲمٕژ، مدینہ ہیٛکہٕ دارالحکومت تہٕ محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم اوس صدر۔ حکمرٲنی ٲس بنیٲدی طورس پیٹھ مسلمانن ہنز دستہٕ منٛز، تہٕ نتیجس منٛز یہٕ اوس اسلامک اصلی دارالحکمہٕ۔ امن تہٕ سلامتی ہنٛد زون بڑھانے خاطرٕ، نبی صلى الله علیه وسلمن کوٚر پننہٕ ریاستس آس پاس روزن وٲل باقی قبیلن سۭتۍ مشابہٕ معاہدٕ کرنہٕ شروع۔

english: The Prophet on the Battlefield The Quraishites, mortified at the escape of the Prophet ﷺ along with his devoted companions, and jealous of his growing power in Madinah, kept a stringent watch over the Muslims left behind and persecuted them in every possible way. They also initiated clandestine contacts with ‘Abdullah bin Uabi bin Salul, chief of Madinese polytheists, and president designate of the tribes ‘Aws and Khazraj before the Prophet’s emigration. They sent him a strongly- worded ultimatum ordering him to fight or expel the Prophet, otherwise they would launch a widespread military campaign that would exterminate his people and proscribe his women.
kashmiri: نبوی جنگہٕ میدانس پیٹھ قریشین، یس نبی صلى الله عليه وسلم سٕندِس فرارس پیٹھ تہندین عقیدت مند ساتھین سٕتۍ غمگین اوس، تہٕ مدینہس منز پننہِ بڑھہٕ وٲل طاقتس پیٹھ حسد اوس، تمو کوٚر پَتہٕ باقی ماندہ مسلمانن پیٹھ سخت نگرانی تہٕ تمن ہر ممکن طریقس سۭتۍ پیچھا۔ تمو کٔر مدینہٕک مشرکین ہند سربراہ عبداللہ بن اوبی بن سلول سٕنٛدس سٕتھ خفیہ رابطٕ تہٕ بنیٲدی صدر عوس تہٕ خزرج سٕنزِ ہجرتہٕ برونٹھ۔ تمن کوٚر سٕنۍ

english: [Narrated by Abu Da'ud]
kashmiri: [ابو داؤد سنٛد بیان]

english: His pride wounded and kingship no longer his, ‘Abdullah bin Uabi bin Salul, a priori responded positively to his Quraishite co- polytheists. He mobilized his supporters to counteract the Muslims. The Prophet ﷺ on hearing about this unholy alliance, summoned ‘Abdullah and admonished him to be more sensible and thoughtful and cautioned his men against being snared in malicious tricks. [Narrated by Abu Da'ud] The men, on grounds of cowardice, or reason, gave up the idea. Their chief, however, seemingly complied, but at heart, he remained a wicked unpredictable accomplice with Quraish and the envious Jews.
kashmiri: امہٕ سٕندِس غرورس زخمی تہٕ بادشاہت اوس نہٕ تہندِ،  عبداللہ بن اوبی بن سلول، اکھ پریتھ وقتس منٛز پننہِ قریشِی شریک مشرکینس سٕتۍ مثبت جواب۔ تمن کوٚر پننہٕ حٲملین مسلمانن خلاف کارروائی کرنہٕ خٲطرٕ متحرک۔ نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن کوٚرمت امہِ ناپسندٕہ اتحادٕ سننہٕ پتہٕ  عَبدو اللہس طلب تہٕ تمن وٲلِتھ زِ تمن ہکو زیادٕ عقلمند تہٕ سوچُن وول تہٕ پننہین لوکن ہینزِ بدسٲلی چالن منز

english: Skirmishes and provocations started to pave the way for a major confrontation between the Muslims and polytheists. Sa‘d bin Mu‘adh, an outstanding Helper, announced his intention to observe ‘Umrah (lesser pilgrimage) and headed for Makkah. There Omaiya bin Khalaf provided tutelage for him to observe the ritual circumambulation. Abu Jahl, an archenemy of Islam saw him in the Sacred Sanctuary and threatened he would have killed him if he had not been in the company of Omaiya.
kashmiri: تِمۍ کوٚر مُسلمانن تہٕ مشرکین درمیان اکھ اہم مقابلہٕچ راہ ہموار۔ سعد بن موجد، اکھ بااثر مددگار، نے عمرہٕ (کم حج) منٲئمک ارادٕچ اعلان تہٕ مکہٕ کہِ طرفہٕ آمت۔ تِہِ منز اوس عمایا بن خالف طریقی محفلہٕ منٲیم کرنہٕ خٲطرٕہ تیمس گٲی ہدایت۔ ابو جہل، اسلامک اکھ دشمنن، اوس سُہ مقدس مقدس منز وچھان تہٕ امس گو دھمکہٕ زِ اگر سُو نہٕ عمایا کہِ صحبتس منز آسہٕ تیلہٕ سُھ سُند قتل کرُ

english: Sa‘d, fearlessly and defiantly, challenged him to committing any folly at the risk of cutting their caravans off.[Bukhari 2/563] Provocative actions continued and Quraish sent the Muslims a note threatening to put them to death in their own homeland. Those were not mere words, for the Prophet ﷺ received information from reliable sources attesting to real intrigues and plots being hatched by the enemies of Islam. Precautionary measures were taken and a state of alertness was called for, including the positioning of security guards around the house of the Prophet ﷺ and strategic junctures.
kashmiri: سعدن، بے خوف تہٕ چیلنجنگ، پننہٕ کاروانن کٹنہٕ کس خطرس سۭتۍ کنہہ تہٕ بیہمتہٕ کرنہٕ خٲطرٕہ سُہٕ چیلینج۔ [بخاری 2/563] پریرتاونک عمل چُھ جاری تہٕ قریشن کوٚر مسلمانن پننہِ وطنس منز قتل کرنُک خطرو سۭتۍ خطرو۔ یہٕ ٲس نہٕ محض الفاظ، کیونکہ نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن آو قابل اعتماد ذرائع سٕتۍ معلومات حٲصل یم اسلامک دشمنی ہنٛد ذریعہٕ اصل سازشات تہٕ سازشن ہنٛد ثبوت دیوان چُھ۔ احتیاطی تدابیر چِھ گٔمٕتۍ تہٕ

english: ‘Aishah رضی اللہ عنہ reported that Allah’s Messenger ﷺ lay down on bed during one night on his arrival in Madinah and said: Were there a pious person from amongst my Companions who should keep a watch for me during the night? She (‘Aishah رضی اللہ عنہ) said: We were in this state when we heard the clanging noise of arms. He (the Prophet ﷺ) said: Who is it? He said: This is Sa‘d bin Abi Waqqas. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ said to him: What brings you here?
kashmiri: عَیِشَہ رَضِیَن زِ رسولَن ہُنْد مَدِینہَس منز راتَس پیٹھ کُنِ چُھ بسترس پیٹھ لٹان۔ سُوٛ وُچھِتھ۔ کیا میرے ساتھیو منٛز چُہ کنہہ خَدایس پرست یُس راتَن مَنٛز رَجَس کَرِتھ؟ سُہ وُہِتھ زِ ہم ٲس ییلہِ ہم ہتھیارن ہُند شور وُنُن۔ سَوٛ گوُن زَن یُن؟ سَسہ وَچھِت: "یہٕ چُھنہ صَد

english: Thereupon he said: I harboured fear (lest any harm should come to) Allah’s Messenger ﷺ, so I came to serve as your sentinel. Allah’s Messenger ﷺ invoked blessings upon him and then he slept.[Muslim 2/280; Bukhari 1/404] This state of close vigilance continued ceaselessly until the Words of Allah were revealed saying: "Allah will protect you from mankind." [Al- Qur'an 5:67] Here, the Prophet ﷺ peeped from the dome of his house asking his people to go away, and making it clear that Allah would take the charge of protecting him.[At-Tirmidhi 2/130]
kashmiri: تمن کوٚر یہٕ باتہٕ زِ مَنٛز چھُ خَشَش (یا خَدایس پیغمبری) پیٹھ تہٕ تمن ہنٛد رَسُول (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) پیٹھ وٲلِتھ، تمن پیٹھ چھُ مَسٲیل (یا نگراں) ، تمن پَتہٕ چھُم خَدِش۔ رسول اللہ صلی اللہ علیہ وسلمن چھُ تمن پرزٕ رحمتہٕ دِوان تہٕ تیم چھےٚ نیٚندٕ۔

english: The Prophet’s life was not the only target of the wicked schemes, but rather the lives and the whole entity of the Muslims. When the Madinese provided the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions with safe refuge, the desert bedouins began to look at them all in the same perspective, and outlawed all the Muslims.
kashmiri: نبی سٕندِس زندگی ہند مقصد اوس نہٕ صرف بدکار منصوبن ہند مقصد بلکہ مسلمانن ہنز زندگی تہٕ پورٕ وجود۔ ییلہِ مدینیو نبی صلى الله عليه وسلم تہٕ تیم سٕنز صحابہٕ سٕتۍ محفوظ پناہ فراہم کٔر، صحرا ہند بدوینو کوٚر تمن ساروی اکس نقطہ نظرس پیٹھ نظر دنہٕ شروع، تہٕ تمو کوٚرن تمام مسلمانن غیر قانونی قرار۔

english: At this precarious juncture with Quraish, intent on pursuing their aggressive and devilish plans, Allah, the All- High, gave the Muslims the permission to take arms against the disbelievers: "Permission to fight is given to those (i.e. believers against those disbelievers), who are fighting them, (and) because they (believers) have been wronged, and surely Allah is Able to give them (believers) victory." [Al- Qur'an 22:39] This verse was revealed in a larger context of Divine instructions to eradicate all aspects of falsehood, and hold in honour the symbols and rites of Allah: "Those (Muslim rulers) who, if We give them power in the land, (they) order for Iqamat- as- Salât: [i.e. to perform Salât (prayer) — the five compulsory, congregational prayers (the males in Mosques)], to pay the Zakat (obligatory charity), and they enjoin Al- Ma‘ruf (i.e.

english: Islamic Monotheism and all that Islam orders one to do), and forbid Al- Munkar (i.e. disbelief, polytheism and all that Islam has forbidden) [i.e. they make the Qur’ân as the Law of their country in all the spheres of life]." [Al- Qur'an 22:41]. Doubtlessly, the permission to fight was revealed in Madinah after emigration, not in Makkah, still the exact date where of is in doubt. The permission to fight was already there, but in the light of the status quo, it was wise for the Muslims to bring the commercial routes leading to Makkah under their control.

english: To realize this strategic objective, the Prophet ﷺ had to choose either of two options:
kashmiri: اتھ حکمت عملی ہنٛد مقصدس حٲصل کرنہٕ خٲطرٕ، نبوی صلى الله عليه وسلمن اوس دۄن اختیارن منٛز اکھ انتخاب کرنس پیٹھ مجبور:

english: a. Entering into non- aggression pacts with the tribes inhabiting either the areas adjacent to the routes or between these routes and Madinah. With respect to this course of action, the Prophet ﷺ had already signed, together with the Jews and other neighbouring tribes, the aforementioned pact of cooperation and good neighbourliness. b. Despatching successive armed missions for harassment along the strategic commercial routs.
kashmiri: a. روٹس سۭتۍ یا یمن روٹس تہٕ مدینہ کہِ درمیان رہن وٲل علاقن منز آباد قبیلن سٕتۍ غٲر جارحیتک معاہدن منز شٲمل۔ اتھ عملس سٕنٛدس سلسلس منز، نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن ٲس یہودیو تہٕ باقی ہمسایہ قبیلین سٕندِس سٔتۍ تعاون تہٕ نیک ہمسٲہی ہند مذکورہٕ معاہدس پیٹھ دستخط کرمُت۔ b. اسٹریٹجک تجارتی روٹس سٕطحس پیٹھ ہیرودٕ خٲطرٕہ متواتر مسلح مشنچ نشٲہی۔

english: Pre-Badr Missions and Invasions With a view to implementing these plans, the Muslims commenced real military activities, which at first took the form of reconnaissance patrols delegated to explore the geopolitical features of the roads surrounding Madinah and others leading to Makkah, and building alliances with the tribes nearby. The Prophet wanted to impress upon the polytheists and Jews of Madinah as well as the bedouins in its vicinity, that the Muslims had smashed their old fears, and had been too strong to be attacked with impunity.
kashmiri: پری بدر مشن تہٕ حملن یمن منصوبہٕن لاگو کرنہٕ خٲطرٕ، مسلمانن کوٚر حقیقی فوجی سرگرمیاں شروع، یم گوڑنچ بارہ منٛز مدینہ تہٕ مکہٕ تام وٲل باقی سڑکن ہنٛز جغرافیائی سیاسی خصوصیات دریافت کرنہٕ خاطرٕ تفویض کرنہٕ آمت جاسوس گشتچ شکلہٕ تھٲو، تہٕ قریبی قبیلن سۭتۍ اتحاد بناونہٕ۔ نبی مڈینہ ہنٛد مشرکین تہٕ یہودین سۭتۍ سۭتۍ امس آس پاسک بدوینن پیٹھ یہٕ واضح کرنہٕ چاہت زِ مسلمانن چُھ پنن پرانین خوفن کچمٕتۍ، تہِ ٲسۍ بے سزا حملس منٛز واریاہ مضبوط۔

english: He also wanted to display the power of his followers in order to deter Quraish from committing any military folly against him which might
kashmiri: سُہٕ اوس پننین پیروکارن ہنٛز طاقتٕ تہٕ ظٲہر کرنٕچ خواہش تھاوان تاکہ قریشس پننس خلاف کُنہٕ تہ فوجی جنون انجام دینہٕ پیٹھ روک تھامٕچ کٲم کرتھ یم امس خلاف کٲفی جنگ بندی کرتھ

english: jeopardize their economic life and means of living, and to stop them from persecuting the helpless Muslims detained in Makkah, consequently he would avail himself of this opportunity and resume his job of propagating the Divine Call freely. The following is a resume of these missions and errands:
kashmiri: یمن ہنٛز معاشی زندگی تہٕ روزنی ہنٛد ذریعہٕ خطرو منٛز ڈالن، تہٕ مکہس منٛز گرفتار بے بس مسلمانن پیٹھ ظلم و ستم کرنٕچ روک تھامٕچ خاطرٕ، امہٕ نتیجس منٛز اوس سُہٕ اتھ موقعس استعمال کران تہٕ دیوی کالچ آزادانہٕ پھیلاونہٕ کس پننہٕ کٲمس دوبارٕہ شروع کران۔

english: 1. Saif Al- Bahr Platoon sent in Ramadan 1 A.H., i.e. 623 A.D. led by Hamzah bin ‘Abdul Muttalib and comprising 30 Emigrants with a definite task of intercepting a caravan belonging to Quraish. It was a caravan of 300 people including Abu Jahl bin Hisham. The two parties encountered each other and aligned in preparation for fighting. Majdi bin ‘Amr, on good terms with both sides, happened to be there and managed to prevent an imminent clash. On that occasion, the Prophet ﷺ accredited the first flag in the history of Muslims.
kashmiri: 1. صائف البحر پلٹون رمضان 1 ہِچ، یعنی 623 عیسوی منز ہمزا بن  عبد مطلِب کہِ سربراہی منز تہٕ 30 مہاجرین پیٹھ مشتمل اوس یہٕ قریش کہِ تعلق تھاوان کاروانس پیٹھ قبضہٕ کرنُک قطعی کامہٕ سٕتۍ۔ یہٕ اوس ابو جہل بن ہشام سٕندِ سٕنٛدس سٕیت 300 لوکن ہند کاروان۔ دۄن جماعتن کوٚر آمتِس مقابلس منز آمت تہٕ لڑنہٕ خٲطرٕ آمت تیاری۔ مجدی بن  ?? عمر، دۄشوَن طرفن سٕنٛزٕ سٲرٕے تعلقاتن پیٹھ،

english: It was white in colour and was entrusted to Kinaz bin Husain AlGhanawi, to carry.
kashmiri: یہٕ اوس سفید رنگس منٛز تہٕ اوس کینیز بن حسین الغنویس سپدان، یمن ہنز نقل کرنہٕ خٲطرٕ۔

english: 2. In Shawwal, 1 A.H., i.e. April 623 A.D. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ despatched ‘Ubaidah bin Al- Harith bin Al- Muttalib at the head of 60 horsemen of Emigrants to a spot called Batn Rabegh where they encountered Abu Sufyan at the head of a caravan of 200 men. There was arrow shooting but no actual fighting. It is interesting to note that two Muslims, Al- Miqdad bin ‘Amr Al- Bahrani and ‘Utbah bin Ghazwan Al- Mazini, defected from the caravan of Quraish and joined the ranks of ‘Ubaidah.
kashmiri: 2۔ شوال، 1 AH، یعنی اپریل 623 AD منٛز، رسول اللہ صلى الله عليه وسلمن کوٚر 60 مہاجرین ہنز گھوڑس پیٹھ بایدہ بن الحارث بن المطالبس پیٹھ باتن ربغ نامی مقامس تام شٲمل، یتزن تمن کوٚرن ابو سفیانس 200 لوکن ہنز کاروانس پیٹھ۔ تیرٕچ فائرنگ اوس آمت مگر نہٕ اصل لڑائی۔ یہٕ چُھ دلچسپ زِ زٕ مسلمان، المقداد بن عمرو البحرانی تہٕ اوتبا بن غزوان المزینی، کرٲیشن ہنز کروان پیٹھہٕ ہجرت تہٕ سُوٛ بیدہ ہ

english: The Muslims had a white flag carried by Mistah bin Athatha bin Al- Muttalib bin ‘Abd Munaf.
kashmiri: مسلمانن اوس اکھ سفید پرچم مسح بن اتھاتا بن المطالب بن ابد منافس پیٹھہٕ تھاوان۔

english: 3. In Dhul Qa‘dah 1 A.H., i.e. May 623 A.D. the Prophet ﷺ despatched Sa‘d bin Abi Waqqas at the head of 20 horsemen, and instructed them not to go beyond Al- Kharrar. After a five- day march they reached the spot to discover that the camels of Quraish had left the day before; their flag, as usual, was white and carried by Al- Miqdad bin ‘Amr. 4. Ghazwa Al- Abwa’ or Waddan. It was in Safar 2 A.H., i.e. 623 A.D.
kashmiri: 3۔ ذوالقذاہ 1 ہِس منز، یعنی 623 ہِسی مئی منز، نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن کٔر 20 گھوڑس پیٹھ سعد بن ابی وقاصس پیٹھ مشن، تہٕ تمن ہدایت زِ وہن نہٕ الخرر پیٹھہٕ گژھہِ۔ پانژہٕ روزن وٲل مارچہٕ پتہٕ تمو کوٚر یہٕ مقامس تام پہنچنہٕ زِ قریش کہ اونٹۍ ٲس وارےاہ۔ یمن ہٕنٛدۍ پرچم، معمولس مطٲبق، اوس سفید تہٕ المیگداد بن عمرو اوس وٲرتھ۔ 4۔ غزوا ال ابوا یا واڈن۔ یہ اوس ص

english: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out himself at the head of 70 men, mostly Emigrants, to intercept a camel caravan belonging to Quraish, leaving behind Sa‘d bin ‘Ubadah to dispose the affairs in Madinah. When he reached Waddan, a place between Makkah and Madinah, he found none. In the process of this campaign, he contracted a non- aggression pact with ‘Amr bin Makhshi Ad- Damari. The provisions of the pact go as follows: "This is a document from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah concerning Bani Damrah in which he established them safe and secure in their wealth and lives.
kashmiri: رسول اللہ صلى الله عليه وسلم گو 70 مٲنس پیٹھ، زیادٕ تر تارکین وطن، قریش کہِ تعلق تھاوان اونٹٕک کاروان روکنہٕ خٲطرٕہ پننِس پیٹھ گام لگاونہٕ، تہٕ سعد بن عوبیدہہس پِھرٕ مَدینہ منز معاملات حل کرنہٕ خٲطرِہ۔ ییلہِ سُہِ مکہٕ تہٕ مکہِ درمیان وڈڈن تام گُزِتھ، تمن کوٚر نہٕ کنہِ تہٕ نہٕ۔ امہٕ مہم کہِ دوران، سُوٛ کر امر بن مخشی اددامری سٕتۍ عدم جارحیتک معاہدہ۔ معاہدٕچ شرائط چِ

english: They can expect support from the Muslims unless they oppose the religion of Allah. They are also expected to respond positively in case the Prophet sought their help.[]" This was the first invasion under the leadership of the Messenger of Allah. It took fifteen days, with a white flag carried by Hamzah bin ‘Abdul Muttalib.
kashmiri: تم ہیکن مسلمانن سۭتۍ مدد توقع کرتھ ییلہٕ زن تمن ہنٛد تعلق اللہ کہ دینس سۭتۍ چُھ نہ۔ اگر پیغمبرن یمن ہنٛز مدد طلب کرتھ تیلہٕ تمن چُہ مثبت جواب دینہٕچ توقع۔" یہٕ اوس رسول اللہ سنٛد قیادتس تحت گوڈنٕک حملہ۔ یہٕ گیہٕ پندرہٕ روزہٕ، حمزہ بن عبدالمطلبس سۭتۍ سفید پرچم۔

english: 5. Buwat Invasion. It took place in Rabi‘ Al- Awwal 2 A.H., i.e. 623 A.D. The Prophet ﷺ, at the head of 200 companions, marched for Buwat to intercept a caravan belonging to Quraish comprising 100 Quraishites, Omaiya bin Khalaf among them, and 2500 camels. When he reached Buwat, the caravan had left. Before leaving Madinah, he mandated Sa‘d bin Mu‘adh to dispose the affairs until his return. 6. Safwan Invasion. In Rabi‘ Al- Awwal 2 A.H., i.e. 623 A.D. Karz bin Jabir at the head of a small group of polytheists raided the pastures of Madinah and looted some animals.
kashmiri: 5. بوات حملہ۔ یہٕ اوس ربی الاوال 2 ہ.د. یعنی 623 ہ.دی. منز آمُت۔ نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن، 200 صحابین ہنز سربراہی سۭتۍ، بواتس تام مارچ کٔرمٕژ تاکہ قریش کہِ تعلق تھاوان کاروانس پیٹھ قابو پَنُن۔ 100 قریشین، یمن منز امہٕ سٕتۍ اومائیہ بن خلف تہٕ 2500 اونٹ۔ جبٕ بوات پَتہٕ آو کاروان چُھ گُمٕژ۔ مدینہ چھوٹنہٕ برونٹھ، سُوٛ سَد بن موہادس امہِ کتھ ہنز انتظام کرنچ مُراد

english: The Prophet ﷺ at the head of 70 men left Madinah to fight the aggressors. He went in their pursuit till he reached a place called Safwan near Badr but could not catch up with them. This invasion came to be known as the preliminary Badr Invasion. During his absence, the Prophet ﷺ entrusted Zaid bin Harithah with the disposition of the affairs in Madinah. The standard was white in colour and entrusted to ‘Ali bin Abi Talib to carry. 7. Dhil ‘Ushairah Invasion. It was in Jumada- al- Ula and Jumada- al- Akhirah the first or second 2 A.H., i.e. November- December 623 A.D.
kashmiri: نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن 70 مینن سربراہن پیٹھ حملہ آورن خلاف جنگ کرنہٕ خٲطرٕہ مڈینہ گٲی۔ تمن پیٹھ چُھ تمن ہینز پیچھا کران یوتتھ تام کہ تمن بدرس قریب صفوان ونان چھ مگر تمن ہیکن نہٕ پکڑتھ۔ یہ حملہ گو ابتدائی بدر حملہٕ کس ناوس سۭتۍ زاننہٕ۔ پننہٕ غٲرضی دوران، نبی صلى اللہ عليه وسلم کوٚر زید بن حریتھ مدینہ منٛز معاملاتن ہنٛد انتظام سپدان۔ سٹینڈر اوس سفید رنگ تہٕ  علی بن ابی طالبس سپدان اوس۔

english: The Prophet ﷺ at the head of 150- 200 Muslim volunteers, with 30 camels which they rode turn by turn, set out to intercept a Quraishite caravan. He reached Dhil ‘Ushairah but the camels had left some days before. These camels were the same that he went out to intercept on their return from Syria, and were the direct reason for the break out of the battle of Badr. In the process of this campaign, the Prophet ﷺ contracted a non- aggression pact with Bani Madlij and their allies Bani Dhumrah.
kashmiri: نبی صلى الله عليه وسلم 150-200 مسلم رضاکارانن ہنز سربراہی منٛز، 30 اونٹین سۭتۍ یم تمن کٔر باری باری پیٹھ سوار، قریشین کاروانن روکنہٕ خٲطرٕہ گو۔ تمن کوٚر دِل اُشیرہ تام پہنچان مگر اونٹۍ ٲس کنہہ روز برونٹھ گمت۔ یم اونٹٕ ٲس یمن ہیو یم تم شامس پیٹھ واپس گژھن پیٹھ روکنہِ خٲطرٕ گٲمٕتۍ، تہٕ بدر کہ جنگچ براہ راست وجہ ٲس۔ اتھ مہمچ عملس منٛز، نبی صلى اللہ عليه وسلم بنی مدلیج تہٕ یمن ہنٛد اتحادیہٕ بنی دھمرا سۭتۍ اکھ عدم جارحیتک معاہدٕ۔

english: Abu Salama bin ‘Abd Al- Asad AlMakhzumi was mandated to rule Madinah in his absence. 8. The Platoon of Nakhlah. It took place in Rajab 2 A.H., i.e. January 624 A.H. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ despatched ‘Abdullah bin Jahsh Asadi to Nakhlah at the head of 12 Emigrants with six camels. ‘Abdullah was given a letter by the Prophet ﷺ but was instructed to read it only after two days.
kashmiri: ابو سلام بن عبدالاسد المخزومی اوس پننہ غٲئبس منٛز مدینہٕ ہنز حکمرٲنی کرنچ ذمہ داری۔ 8. نکھلا ہنز پلٹن۔ یہٕ گٔیہ راجاب 2 اے ایچ، یعنی جنوری 624 اے ایچی منز۔ رسول اللہ صلى الله عليه وسلمن کوٚر 12 تارکین وطنن سٕتۍ چھ اونٹہٕ سٕنٛدس سربراہی منٛز عبداللہ بن جاش اسدی نکھلہٕ منٛز بھیج۔  عبداللہس آو رسول صلى الله علیه وسلم سٕندِس طرفہٕ اکھ خط دِنہٕ مگر تمن آو یہٕ صرف زٕ روزن پتہٕ پڑھنہٕ خٲطرٕ ہدایت۔

english: He followed the instructions and discovered that he was asked to go on to a place called Nakhlah standing between Makkah and At- Ta’if, intercept a caravan for Quraish and collect news about their intentions. He disclosed the contents of the letters to his fellows who blindly obeyed the orders. At Nakhlah, the caravan passed carrying loads of raisins (dried grapes), food stuff and other commodities. Notable polytheists were also there such as ‘Amr bin Al- Hadrami, ‘Uthman and Naufal, sons of ‘Abdullah bin Al- Mugheerah and others...
kashmiri: تیمو کوٚر ہدایاتچ پیروی تہٕ پتہ چلا کہ تیمس آو مکہٕ تہٕ ات تیف کہِ درمیان کھڑا اکھ مقام نکھلہ ونانہٕ خٲطرٕہ وٲل کرنہٕ تہِ قریش خٲطرٕ اکھ کاروان روکنہٕ تہ تہٕ یمن ہنٛدین اراداتن متعلق خبریں جمع کرنہٕ۔ تیمو کٔر پننین ساتھین خٲطرٕ یم اندھیرا حکمچ اطاعت کران یمن لیکھن ہند مواد ظاہر۔ نکھلاہس منز، کاروانن گٲی راسن (سختہ انگور) ، خوراکک سامان تہٕ باقی سامانن ہند بوجھ لے کر۔ مشہور مشرکین تہٕ ٲسۍ یمن منز زَن امر بن الحدری

english: The Muslims held consultations among themselves with respect to fighting them taking into account Rajab which was a sacred month (during which, along with Dhul Hijja, Dhul Qa‘da and Muharram, war activities were suspended as was the custom in Arabia then). At last they agreed to engage with them in fighting. ‘Amr bin Al- Hadrami was shot dead by an arrow, ‘Uthman and Al- Hakam were captured whereas Naufal escaped. They came back with the booty and the two prisoners. They set aside one- fifth of the booty assigned to Allah and His Messenger, and took the rest.
kashmiri: مسلمانن کوٚر تمن سۭتۍ جنگہٕ خٲطرٕ مشاورت، رجب کہِ مقدس مہینہٕ کہِ حسابس منز۔ (یتھ دوران ذوالحجّہ، ذوالقعدہ تہِ محرم سٕتۍ جنگہِ ہنز سرگرمی معطل گیٔی، یتھ کٔنۍ عربس منز اوس عام) ۔ آخرکار تمو وٲتِم زِ تمن سٕندِس جنگس منز حصہٕ ننہٕ۔ امر بن الحدریمی سٕنٛدس اوس تیرٕ سٕنٛز مارنہٕ آمُت، اُثمان تہٕ حکم آو گرفتار کرنہٕ تہٕ نُفال چُھ فرار۔ تمو آو غ

english: The Messenger disapproved of that act and suspended any action as regards the camels and the two captives on account of the prohibited months already mentioned. The polytheists, on their part, exploited this golden opportunity to calumniate the Muslims and accuse them of violating what is Divinely inviolable. This idle talk brought about a painful headache to Muhammad’s Companions, until at last they were relieved when the Revelation came down giving a decisive answer and stating quite explicitly that the behaviour of the polytheists in the whole
kashmiri: رسولن کوٚر اتھ عملس پیٹھ ناراض تہٕ تمن دوٛن قیدین پیٹھ پابندی لگا دیت، یمن مہینن پیٹھ چھِ پابندی عائد۔ مشرکینن کوٚرن امہٕ موقعہٕ استعمال تاکہ مسلمانن پیٹھ بدسلوکی کرتھ تہٕ یمن پیٹھ خدائی حرام چیزس خلاف الزام لگاون۔ یہٕ بیہٕ باتہٕ کوٚر محمد (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) سٕندین ساتھین پیٹھ دردناک دردٕچ وجہ تہٕ یوتام زِ وحی نازل گژھِتھ تمن پیٹھ اکھ فیصلہ کن جواب تہٕ یہٕ واضح طور پٲنٹھ بیان کران کہ تمام مشرکین ہنٛد عمل چُھ

english: process was much more heinous and far more serious than the act of the Muslims: "They ask you concerning fighting in the sacred months (i.e. 1st, 7th, 11th and 12th months of the Islamic calendar). Say, ‘Fighting therein is a great (transgression) but a greater (transgression) with Allah is to prevent mankind from following the way of Allah, to disbelieve in Him, to prevent access to Al- Masjid- Al- Harâm (at Makkah), and to drive out its inhabitants, and Al- Fitnah is worse than killing." [AlQur'an 2:217] The Words of Allah were quite clear and said that the tumult created by the polytheists was groundless.
kashmiri: تم چھہِ تمس پیٹھ مقدس مہینن منز لڑنُک سوال کران، تم چھیہ یہ کہ تمن منز جنگ چھیس اکھ عظیم گناہ، مگر خداس نزدیک چھیو یہ کہ انسانن خدا کہِ راستہ پیٹھ نہ چھیوسہِ، تہ تم اسہِ پیٹھ نہ ایمان آسہِ تہ مسجدِ حرامس پیٹھ نہ آسہٕ، تہ تہ تمس منز روزن والن ہٹانا، تہ فتنہ چھہ قتلس کھوتہٕ بدتر۔

english: The sacred inviolable sanctities had been repeatedly violated in the long process of fighting Islam and persecuting its adherents. The wealth of the Muslims as well as their homes had already been violated and their Prophet ﷺ had been the target of repeated attempts on his life. In short, that sort of propaganda could deservedly be described as impudence and prostitution. This has been a resume of pre- Badr platoons and invasions. None of them witnessed any sort of looting property or killing people except when the polytheists had committed such crimes under the leadership of Karz bin Jabir Al- Fahri.
kashmiri: مقدس ناقابلِ نقاب مقدسات ٲس اسلامس خلاف جنگ کرن تہٕ امس پیٹھ عمل کرنک طویل عملس منٛز وار وار وار خلاف ورزی کرنہٕ آمت۔ مسلمانن ہنٛز دولت تہٕ یمن ہنٛد مکانات ٲس وار وارٕ وار خلاف ورزیدٕ آمٕتۍ تہٕ تمن ہنٛد نبی صلى الله عليه وسلم اوس تیمس پیٹھ وارٕ بار زندگی ہنٛد کوششک نشانہٕ۔ مختصر طور پأنٹھ، اتھ قسمک پروپیگنڈہٕ ہیکن حقس سۭتۍ بے وقوفیت تہٕ فحشگناہی کہٕ طورس پیٹھ بیان کرنہٕ یوان۔ یہٕ چُھ بدر برونٹھ پلاٹن تہٕ حملن ہنٛز ایکہٕ سیریز۔ یمن منٛز کنہہ تہٕ نہٕ چِھ کنہہ

english: It was, in fact, the polytheists who had initiated such acts. No wonder, for such ill- behaviour is immanent in their natural disposition. Shortly afterwards, the two captives were released and blood money was given to the killed man’s father.[For details see Za'd Al-Ma'ad 2/83-85; Ibn Hisham 1/605; Rahmat-ul-lil'alameen 1/115, 2/468] After this event, Quraish began to realize the real danger that Madinah could present with. They came to know that Madinah had always been on the alert, watching closely their commercial caravans.
kashmiri: یہٕ اوس، حقیقتس منٛز، مشرکین یمن ہنٛدین عملن ہنٛد آغاز کوٚر۔ یہٕ چُھ نہٕ تعجب کن، کیونکہ امہٕ قسمک بدسلوکی چُہ یمن ہنٛز فطری نوعیتس منٛز غٲر غٲب۔ تھوڑی دیر پتہٕ، یمن زٕ قیدیو آو آزاد کرنہٕ تہٕ خونچ پیسے قتل گژھن وٲل سٕنٛدس باپتھ دینہٕ۔ [تفصیلن خٲطرٕہ زعید المعاد 2/83-85؛ ابن ہشام 1/605؛ رحمت-ال-ل-علامین 1/115, 2/468] اتھ واقعہٕ پتہٕ کور قریشن اصل خطرٕ محسوس زِ مدینہٕ آس

english: It was then common knowledge to them that the Muslims in their new abode could span and extend their military activities over an area of 300 miles. and bring it under full control. However, the new situation borne in mind, the Makkans could not be deterred and were too obstinate to come to terms with the new rising power of Islam. They were determined to bring their fall by their own hands and with this recklessness they precipitated the great battle of Badr.
kashmiri: تمن اوس تہندین نوین رہائش گاہن منٛز مسلمانن عام علم زِ تم ہیکن پننین فوجی سرگرمیہٕ 300 میلس پیٹھ پھیلاون تہٕ بڑھاون تہِ اتھ مکمل کنٹرولس منٛز آسن۔ تاہم، نوین حالاتن ہنٛد خیال تھاوان، مککنن ہیکن نہٕ روکاونہٕ تہٕ اسلامک نٔوین بڑھن وٲل طاقتس سۭتۍ نمٹنہٕ خٲطرٕ ٲسۍ واریاہ ضد۔ تم ٲسۍ پننہٕ پانہٕ پننِ ہاتھوں پننٕس خاتمٕچ کوشش کرنک قائل تہٕ اتھ غفلتس سۭتۍ تمو کوٚر بدر کہ عظیم جنگچ جلدی۔

english: The Muslims, on the other hand, and at the behest of their Lord, were ordered to go to war in Sha‘ban 2 A.H: "And fight, in the way of Allah those who fight you; but transgress not the limits. Truly, Allah likes not the transgressors. And kill them wherever you find them, and turn them out from where they have turned you out. And AlFitnah (polytheism or calamity) is worse than killing. And fight not with them at Al- Masjid- Al- Harâm (the Sanctuary at Makkah), unless they (first) fight you there. But if they attack you, then kill them.
kashmiri: مسلمانن ہند پروردگارس حکم اوس اوس اوسژھ زِ شَبان (شعبان) منز (دُور) گژھہِ تہ تمن سان جنگ کرن والن ہندین (دشمن) پیٹھ ، مگر تمن خلاف نہ کٔرِتھ ۔ بے شک خدا چُھ تمن زیادٔہ حدس پیٹھہ نہ رُوزان ۔ تمن پیٹھ ییہِ کتھہٕ تہِ گژھِتھ قتل ، تمن پانس پیٹھ تمن ہندين پیٹھ چُھنہِ کتہٕ ، تہِ فتنہٕ چُہ قتلس پیٹھ بدتر ، تمہِ سان مسجدِ حرامس منز نہ لڑو مگر ییلہِ تمن پیٚٹھہ تمن سے لڑو

english: Such is the recompense of the disbelievers. But if they cease, then Allah is OftForgiving, Most Merciful. And fight them until there is no more Fitnah (disbelief and worshipping of others along with Allah) and (all and every kind of ) worship is for Allah (Alone). But if they cease, let there be no transgression except against Az- Zalimûn (polytheists, and wrong- doers, etc.)" [Al- Qur'an 2:190- 193]
kashmiri: یِہ چُھ نہٕ یِنٛہٕ خأطرِ یِم نَفَس پیٹھ نِنہٕ وَنان۔ اگر یہِ سرکش چِھ، تہٕ خدا چُہ معاف کرٕن وٲل تہٕ رحم کرٕنۍ، تہندِس خلاف جنگ کرو یوتتھ تام زِ فتنہٕ نہٕ گژھہِ تہٕ عبادت تہٕ خۄدائے خُدائےِ سٲر ہیو۔ اگر تم یہِ ترک کرِتھ، تہِ زِیمن تہٕ بدکارن ہیو نہٕ زیادٕہ مہیٚکان۔"

english: Before long, Allah again sent the Muslims a different sort of verses whereby teaching them ways of fighting, urging them to go to war and demonstrating relevant rules: "So, when you meet (in fight - Jihâd in Allah’s cause), those who disbelieve smite at their necks till when you have killed and wounded many of them, then bind a bond firmly (on them, i.e. take them as captives). Thereafter (is the time) either for generosity (i.e. free them without ransom), or ransom (according to what benefits Islam), until the war lays down its burden.
kashmiri: تمن پیٹھ آیہِ کتھہِ ہنز کتھِ ہرگاہ نازل۔ تمن ہندِس کتھَس پیٹھ چُھ تمن کتھ کِس بارس منز کتھ کرنہٕ آمُت۔ ییلہِ تمن منز واریاہ لوک مارنہٕ تہٕ زخمی گژھنہٕ آمت، تمن پٔتِس پیٹھ کنہِ کنہٕ کنہُم کنہ کنہ وٲلِتھ۔ امہِ پتہٕ چُہ یا تہِ یا تہٕ فدیہٕ کَرِتھ یا تہُنِس وقتس منز (یہِ) تمن ہنز جنگ ختم گژھِتھ

english: Thus [you are ordered by Allah to continue in carrying out Jihâd against the disbelievers till they embrace Islam (i.e. are saved from the punishment in the Hell- fire) or at least come under your protection], but if it had been Allah’s Will, He Himself could certainly have punished them (without you). But (He lets you fight), in order to test you, some with others. But those who are killed in the way of Allah, He will never let their deeds be lost. He will guide them and set right their state.
kashmiri: تمو کوٚر یہ حکم زِ تمن ہنٛدس بارس منٛز تمن ہنٛز کٲم گژھہِ نہٕ آسان، یوتتھ تام زِ تیم چِھ اسلام قبول کران۔ اگر خدا وند آسہٕ تہٕ تہندین (لوکن) پیٹھ عذاب نازل آسہِ، تہٕ یہٕ چُھ تمہِ خأطرِ یمہٕ خٲطرٕہ آسان، تاکہ تمن منٛز کیہہ تہٕ کیہہ امتحان آسہُن مگر یمو تہندین خاندانس منز قتل گژھان چھئي تمن ہنٛدس بارس منٛز چھنہ تمس پننہ کردار ادا گژھان۔ تمن چھنھ خداے سٕندِس مرضی مطٲبق پننین کردار ادا کران۔

english: And admit them to Paradise which He has made known to them (i.e. they will know their places in Paradise more than they used to know their houses in the world). O you who believe!
kashmiri: تہ تمن آو جنتس منز داخل کرنہٕ یُس خداو تمن کنہٕ تہندین علمس منٛز چُھ آسان۔ اے ایمان والو!

english: If you help (in the cause of) Allah, He will help you, and make your foothold firm." [Al- Qur'an 47:4- 7][Tafheem -ul-Qur'an 5/11] Shortly afterwards, Allah began to dispraise the hypocrites, the weak at heart and cowardly elements: "But when a decisive Sûrah (explaining and ordering things) is sent down, and fighting (Jihâd — the holy fighting) is mentioned (i.e. ordained) therein, you will see those in whose hearts is a disease (of hypocrisy) looking at you with a look of one fainting to death. " [Al- Qur'an 47:20] The prevalent exigencies required as a top priority exhorting the Muslims to fight.
kashmiri: اگر تم خداس پیٹھ (دُستور) گژھِتھ تہٕ تمن مدد کرتھ تہ تمن ہنٛز مدد کرُن تہٕ تُمہٕ پننِس پاٹھ مضبوط کرُتھ۔" تمہِ منز تہِ ہیکہِ تمہِ دلہِ پیٹھ کینٛہہ تہِ کینٛہہ مرضہٕ (منافق) وُچھتھ تمن پیٹھ تہِ چِھہِ وُنِس مرنس تام بے بس گژھن وٲل نظرِ سیتۍ۔"

english: Any leader with a deep insight would order his soldiers to get ready for any sort of emergency, let alone the All- Knowing Exalted Lord, Who is at all times omniscient of the minutest details of affairs. The event of that skirmish with the polytheists dealt a heavy blow to the pride of Quraish and created a sort of horrible restlessness amongst them. The aforementioned Qur’ânic verses, enjoining the Muslims to strive in the cause of Allah, betrayed the proximity of blood clashes that would be crowned by a decisive victory for the Muslims, and final expulsion of polytheists out of the Sacred City, Makkah.
kashmiri: ہر اکھ باصلاحیت رہنما چُھ پننین فوجیو سٕتۍ وٲلِتھ کہ تم چُہ ہر قسمک ہنگامی صورتحال خٲطرٕہ تیار گژھتھ، مگر خداےِ سٕندِس بارس منز چُھنہٕ یہٕ حکم زِ تمام حالاتن ہند ہر وقت چُھ۔ مشرکین سٕنٛدس ساتھ یہٕ لڑائی کور قریش سٕنز غرورس سخت نقصان تہٕ یمن منٛز اکھ قسمک خوفناک بے چینی پٔدٕ۔ مذکورہ قرآنک آیاتن منز چِھ مسلمانن خدا کہِ راہس منز جدوجہد کرنچ ہدایت کران، یہٕ چُس خونہٕ ہنز نزولس پیٹھ غداری کران یم مسلمان

english: They referred to rules pertinent to the treatment of captives and slaughtering the pagan soldiers till the war ended and laid down its burdens. All of these could act as clues to a final triumph that would envelop the strife of the Muslims towards their noble objectives. Another event of great significance featured the same month Sha‘ban 2 A.H., i.e. February 624 A.D., which was a Divine injunction ordering that Al- Qiblah be changed from Jerusalem to the Sacred Mosque in Makkah. That was of a great advantage to the Muslims at two levels.
kashmiri: تمن کوٚر جنگہٕ تام قٲبلہِ قٲئم قواعدن ہنٛد حوالہٕ تہٕ جنگہِ تام غیرمسیحی فوجیو ذبح کرنس متعلق۔ یہٕ تمام ہیکن اکھ حتمی فتحک اشارے کِس طورس پیٹھ کٲم کٔرتھ یم مسلمانن ہنٛز جنگ یمن ہنٛدِ نٔبلس مقاصدس پیٹھ چِھ احاطہ کران۔ اکھ بیاکھ اہم واقعہٕ اوس اَتھ مہینہِ شابان 2 اے ایچ، یعنی 624 عیسوی کہِ فروری منز، یس اکھ الہی حکم اوس یوس حکم اوس دیُت زِ القیبہٕ یروشلمس پیٹھہٕ مکہٕ کہِ مقدس مسجدس منز تبدیل کرنہٕ۔ یہ

english: First, it brought about a kind of social sifting, so to speak, in terms of the hypocrites of the Jews and others weak at heart, and revealed their true nature and inclinations; the ranks of the Muslims were thereby purged from those discord- prone elements. Second, facing a new Qiblah, the Sacred Mosque in Makkah, refers gently to a new role awaiting the Muslims to take up, and would start
kashmiri: گوڈنٕک، یہٕ کوٚر یہٕ یہودیو تہٕ باقی دلک کمزور منافقن ہنٛدس لحاظ سۭتۍ اکھ قسمک سمأجی چھانٹنہٕ، یتھ کٔنۍ زن ونان، تہٕ یمن ہنٛز حقیقی نوعیت تہٕ رجحاناتچ نشاندہی۔ امہٕ سۭتۍ آیہٕ مسلمانن ہنٛز صفہٕ یمن اختلافن ہند عناصرن سۭتۍ پاک کرنہٕ۔ دوٚیم، اکھ نٔوِس قبلہٕ، مکہٕ منٛز مقدس مسجدس سۭتۍ آمت، ہلکی سان مسلمانن ہینز توقع تھون وٲل اکھ نٲو کردارُک حوالہٕ دیوان، تہِ یہٕ شروع گژھت

english: only after the repatriation of the Muslims to their Sacred City, Makkah for it is not logical for the Muslims to leave their Qiblah at the mercy of non- Muslims. The Muslims, therefore, at the behest of Allah and on account of those Divine clues, augmented their activities and their tendency towards striving in the cause of Allah and encountering His enemies in a decisive battle were greatly intensified.
kashmiri: مگر تمن ہنٛد وطن واپس گژھنہٕ پتہٕ، مکہٕ، نہٕ یہٕ چُھ مسلمانن خٲطرٕہ مناسب زِ تمن ہنٛز قبیلہٕ نہٕ غیر مسلمن ہنٛد رحم سۭتۍ چھوڑن۔ امہٕ وجہ سۭتۍ، تمن کوٚر خدا کہ حکمس پیٹھ تہٕ خدا کہِ ذٲتی ہند وجہ سۭتۍ زیادٕہ تر کوشش تہٕ تمن خۄدا کہِ راہس منز جہاد تہٕ اسہٕ کہِ دشمنن پیٹھ سخت لڑائی منٛز اضافہ۔

english: The Battle of Badr The First Decisive Battle in the History of Islam Reason of the Battle We have already spoken about Al- ‘Ushairah Invasion when a caravan belonging to Quraish had escaped an imminent military encounter with the Prophet ﷺ and his men. When their return from Syria approached, the Prophet ﷺ despatched Talhah bin ‘Ubaidullâh and Sa‘id bin Zaid northward to scout around for any movements of this sort. The two scouts stayed at Al- Hawra’ for some days until Abu Sufyan, the leader of the caravan, passed by them.
kashmiri: بدر کہِ جنگ اسلام کہِ تاریخس منز گوڈنِکہِ فیصلہ کن جنگ جنگ جنگِ ہند وجہ ہمن گوڈٕ الٰٰٰہِشہِ ہنز غزوہٕ پیٹھ کتھ کرنہٕ ییلہِ قریش کہِ تعلق تھاوان اکھ کاروان اوس نبی صلى الله عليه وسلم تہٕ تیم سٕندِس لوکن سٕتۍ گژھن وٲلِس قریب فوجی مُلاقاتس منز فرار۔ ییلِہِ تیم سُند واپسی شامہٕ سٕنٛدِ قریب آیہِ، نبی صلى اللہ عليه وسلمن سُوٛ تلہ بن عوبید اللہ تہٕ سٲید بن زاید شمالس تام اتھ قسمک کنہِ تہٕ حرکتن

english: The two men hurried back to Madinah and reported to the Prophet ﷺ their findings. Great wealth amounting to 50 thousand gold Dinars guarded by 40 men moving relatively close to Madinah constituted a tempting target for the Muslim military, and provided a potentially heavy economic, political and military strike that was bound to shake the entire structure of the Makkan polytheists. The Prophet ﷺ immediately exhorted the Muslims to rush out and waylay the caravan to make up for their property and wealth they were forced to give up in Makkah.
kashmiri: تمن زٕ لوکن ہٕنٛدس شٲمل گژھنہٕ خٲطرٕ ٲسۍ مسلمان فوجن خٲطرٕ اکھ پرجوش ہدف، تہٕ یہٕ کٔر ممکنہ طورس پیٹھ اکھ بھڑ معاشی، سیاسی تہٕ فوجی حملہٕ یُس مکہٕ کہ مشرکین ہنٛز پورٕ ساخت ہلاونہٕ خٲطرِ پابند اوس۔ نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمن ژر مسلمانن زور دیُت زِ تمن ہنٛز جائیداد تہٕ مالک تلافی کرنہٕ خٲطرُک کاروانن ہینز جلدی برونٹھ تہٕ وائیلائی۔

english: He did not give orders binding to everyone, but rather gave them full liberty to go out or stay back, thinking that it would be just an errand on a small scale. The Muslim army was made up of 300- 317 men, 82- 86 Emigrants, 61 from Aws and 170 from Khazraj. They were not well- equipped nor adequately prepared. They had only two horses belonging to Az- Zubair bin Al- ‘Awwam and Al- Miqdad bin Al- Aswad Al- Kindi, 70 camels, one for two or three men to ride alternatively.
kashmiri: امہٕ کوٚر نہٕ تمام لوکن خٲطرٕ پابند احکامات، بلکہ تمن آو مکمل آزادی دیتھ کہ یہٕ برونٹھ چُھ یا واپس رہتھ، یہٕ خیال کرتھ کہ ییہٕ چُہ صرف اکھ چھوٹہٕ پیمانس پیٹھ کامہٕ۔ مسلم فوج ٲس 300-317 مرد، 82-86 تارکین وطن، 61 آوٕس تہٕ 170 خزرج۔ تم ٲس نہٕ پورٕ تییہٕ تیار۔ تمن اوس صرف ز زبیر بن الاوام تہٕ المقداد بن الاسواد الکندی ہنز دوہ گھوڑ، 70 اونٹ، دوہٕ یا ترٕ مردن خٲطرٕ اکھ متبادل طور پٲنٹھ سوار۔

english: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ himself, ‘Ali and Murthid bin Abi Murthid Al- Ghanawi had only one camel. Disposition of the affairs of Madinah was entrusted to Ibn Umm Maktum but later to Abu Lubabah bin ‘Abdul Mundhir. The general leadership was given to Mus‘ab bin ‘Umair Al- Qurashi Al- ‘Abdari, and their standard was white in colour. The little army was divided into two battalions, the Emigrants with a standard raised by ‘Ali bin Abi Talib, and the Helpers whose standard was in the hand of Sa‘d bin Mu‘adh.
kashmiri: رسول اللہ صلى الله عليه وسلم سٕندِس سٕنٛدۍ سٕنٛز، علی تہٕ مرثید بن ابی مرثيد الگھانوی سٕنز اوس صرف اکھ اونٹ۔ مدینہٕ ہٕنٛز معاملاتن ہٕنٛد انتظام اوس ابن ام مقتومس سپدان مگر پتہٕ ابو لوبا بن ابدُل منڈیرس۔ عام قیادت اوس موساب بن ٗومیر القراشی الابدیرس سپدان، تہٕ یمن ہٕنز پرچم اوس سفید رنگ۔ چھوٹی فوج ٲس زٕ بیٹالین منٛز تقسیم کرنہٕ آمت، امیگریٹ یم سٕتۍ  علی بن ابیب طالب سٕن پرچم چُھ ا

english: Az- Zubair bin Al- ‘Awwam was appointed to the leadership of the right flank, AlMiqdad bin ‘Amr to lead the left flank, and the rear of the army was at the command of Qais bin Abi Sa‘sa‘ah. The General Commander- in- Chief was the Prophet ﷺ, of course. The Prophet ﷺ, at the head of his army, marched out along the main road leading to Makkah. He then turned left towards Badr and when he reached As- Safrâ’, he despatched two men to scout about for the camels of Quraish. Abu Sufyan, on the other hand, was on the utmost alert.
kashmiri: از-زبیر بن العوام اوس دٲنی فلانک قیادت، المقدد بن عمرو پیٹھ دٲم کرنہٕ آمت، تہٕ فوجچ پیٹھہٕ ٲس قیس بن ابی ساسہاہس حکمس تحت۔ جنرل کمانڈر-ن-چیف اوس نبی صلى الله عليه وسلم، یقیناً۔ نبی صلى اللہ عليه وسلم پننہ فوجک سربراہس پیٹھ، مککہٕ کہِ مرکزی سڑکس پیٹھہِ مارچ۔ پتہٕ بٲڑس طرفہٕ چُھ سُہ بائیں مڑان تہٕ ییلہٕ سُوٛ آس سفراہس تام گٲی، تمن کٔر قریش کہِ اونٹٕچ تلاش کرنہٕ خٲطرٕ

english: He had already been aware that the route he was following was attended with dangers. He was also anxious to know about the movements of Muhammad ﷺ. His scouting men submitted to him reports to the effect that the Muslims were lying in ambush for his caravan. To be on the safe side, he hired Damdam bin ‘Amr Al- Ghifari to communicate a message asking for help from the Quraishites. The messenger rode fast and reached Makkah in frenzy.
kashmiri: سُہٕ اوس گوڑنک تام یہٕ زانان زِ سُوٛ چُھ یہٕ روٹ خطرن سۭتۍ وابستہٕ۔ سُھ محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم کہِ حرکتن ہنز جانس خٲطرٕہ تہٕ بے چینی۔ سٕندِس سکاٹ مینو کوٚر سُند اطلاعہٕ سٕتۍ یہٕ کہ مسلمان چِھ سُنٛدیٚن کاروانن خٲطرٕ کمینس منز پَھلمت۔ محفوظ طرفہٕ گژھنہٕ خٲطرٕ، سُٛو کُرمٕت دَمدام بن امر الغفاری قریشین سٕنٛدس مددٕ خٲطرِ اکھ پیغامٕہٕ دِوان۔

english: Felling himself from his camel, he stood dramatically before Al- Ka‘bah, cut off the nose and the ears of the camel, turned its saddle upside down, tore off his own shirt from front and behind, and cried: "O Quraish! Your merchandise! It is with
kashmiri: اَمِ کَمۍ سٔتی سٔتۍ گٔمِس سٔتِس کَمہِ پیٹھ اَتھ کَتھِ پیٹھ کَرُن ۔ سَپدِتھ تٔ سٔنْزِ چُھس سَرٔ پَتٔ تٔ اَکھ

english: Abu Sufyan. The caravan is being intercepted by Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. I cannot say what would have happened to them. Help! Help!" The effect of this hue and cry was instantaneous and the news stunned Quraish and they immediately remembered their pride that was wounded when the Muslims had intercepted Al- Hadrami caravan. They therefore swiftly mustered almost all of their forces and none stayed behind except Abu Lahab, who delegated someone who owed him some money. They also mobilized some Arab tribes to contribute to the war against the Prophet ﷺ. All the clans of Quraish gave their consent except Banu ‘Adi.
kashmiri: ابو سفیان۔ محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم تہٕ تیم سٕندین ساتھیو چھ کاروان روکنہٕ یوان۔ میںہ ہیٚکہٕ نہٕ یہٕ ونان زِ یمن سۭتۍ کیا گژھہِ۔ مدد! مدد!" اتھ رنگس تہٕ چیخٕچ اثر اوس فوری تہٕ خبرن کٔر قریش حیران تہٕ تمن اوس ژٕ پننہٕ غرور یاد آمت ییلہٕ مسلمانن الہدرامی کاروانک روکنہ۔ تمو کوٚر ژٕر تقریباً پننہِ فوج جمع تہٕ نہ ہیٚکو کنہِ باقی مگر ابو لہب، یس سُہٕ سٕنٛدس کنہٕ تہٕ پیسے قرضہٕ تھاوان اوس۔ تمن

english: Soon an excited throng of 1300 soldiers including 100 horsemen and 600 mailed soldiers with a large number of camels, was clamouring to proceed to fight the Muslims. For food supplies, they used to slaughter an alternate number of camels of ten and nine every day. They were however afraid that Banu Bakr, on account of old long deep- seated animosity, would attack their rear.
kashmiri: ژور ہیٚکہ 1300 فوجیو سٕتۍ اکھ پرجوش ہجوم یتھ منز 100 گھوڑسوار تہٕ 600 میل شدہ فوجیو تہٕ واریاہ تعدادس سۭتۍ اونٹہٕ تہٕ ٲسۍ مسلمانن سۭتۍ لڑنہٕ خٲطرٕہ چیٹان۔ خوراکٕچ سپلائی خٲطرٕ ٲس تم روزانہٕ پٲنٹھ دس تہٕ نو اونٹٕ ہینز متبادل تعداد ذبح کران۔ تاہم تمن اوس ڈر زِ بانو بکر، پرٛیٚو وٲل طویل عرصس تام گہری دشمنی ہنٛد وجہ سۭتۍ، یمن پیٹھ حملہٕ کرتھ۔

english: At that critical moment, Iblis (Satan) appeared to them in the guise of Suraqa bin Malik bin Ju‘sham Al- Mudlaji — chief of Bani Kinana — saying to them: "I guarantee that no harm will happen from behind." They set out burning with indignation, motivated by a horrible desire for revenge and exterminating anyone that might jeopardize the routes of their caravans: "…boastfully and to be seen of men, and hinder (men) from the path of Allah.
kashmiri: اَتھ اہم وقتس منز، بنی کِنَنَس کہِ سربراہ سُرقا بن مالک بن جُوشام المُدالجی سٕندِ روپَس منز تمن پَتہٕ آو۔ تمن ووٚن زِ "مَن چھُ تمن گٲیِتھ زِ نہٕ کنہٕ پیٹھہٕ کانٛہہ نقصان آسہٕ۔" تمن اوس بغاوتس سٔتۍ جَرٕدٕ، بدلہٕ خأطرٕ خوفناک خواہش سۭتۍ جَلَس تہٕ تمن ہنٛدس قافلس سٔتی خطرہٕ دِنہٕ خٲطرٕہ ہر وَنُک ذٔریعہٕ قَتِل۔

english: " [Al- Qur'an 8:47] Or as the Prophet ﷺ said: "O Allah these are the haughty and conceited; they have come defying Allah and defying His Messenger." They moved swiftly northward to Badr. On the way they received another message from Abu Sufyan asking them to go back home because the caravan had escaped the Muslims. Incidentally, Abu Sufyan, on learning the intention of the Muslims, led his caravan off the main route, and inclined it towards the Red Sea. By this manoeuvre, he was able to slip past the Madinese ambush and was out of their reach.
kashmiri: " [قرآن 8:47] یا یتھ پٲٹھۍ نبی صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم ونےو: "اے اللہ، یہٕ چِھ تمن بڑبڑان تہ مغرور۔ تمن آو اللہ تہٕ تمن رُسولس پیٹھ اعتراض۔" تمن کٔر تیزی سان شمالس تام بدر۔ راستےس پیٹھ آیہٕ ابو سفیانن پیٚٹھ اکھ بیاکھ پیغام حٲصل ییلہٕ تمو پننہٕ وطن واپس گژھنک حکم اوس دیتمُت، کیازِ کاروان مسلمانن پیٹھ چھٹکارہٕ۔ امہٕ پتہٕ ابو صوفیانن، مسلمانن ہینز نیت سٕتۍ، پننہِ کاروانی ساروی کھوتہٕ اہم روٹ پیٹھ

english: On receiving Abu Sufyan’s message, the Makkan army showed a desire to return home. The tyrant Abu Jahl, however haughtily and arrogantly insisted that they proceed to Badr, stay three nights there for making festivities. Now they wanted to punish the Muslims and prevent them from intercepting their caravans, and impress on the Arabs that Quraish still had the upper hand and enjoyed supremacy in that area. Abu Jahl’s threats and insistence notwithstanding, Banu Zahrah, acting on the advice of Al- Akhnas bin Shuraiq, broke away and returned to Makkah.
kashmiri: ابو سفیانن پیغام ملنہٕ پتہٕ، مکہٕ کیٛن فوجن کوٚر پننہٕ وطن واپس گژھنک خواہش ظاہر۔ طاغوت ابو جہل، اگرچہ مغرور تہٕ مغرور طورس پیٹھ اصرار زِ تمن بادرس تام چُھ جٲری، تہٕ تہوار بناونس خٲطرٕہ ترٛی راتہٕ تہٕ روزان۔ اب تہٕ تم ٲسۍ مسلمانن سزا دِنہٕ تہِ یمن ہنٛد کاروانن پیٹھ مداخلت کرنہٕ خٲطرٕ روک تھامٕچ خواہش تھاوان، تہِ عربن پیٹھ چھا یہٕ تاثر دِوان کہ قریشس اوس وآریا تہٕ اتھ علاقس منٛز چھس غالب۔ ابو جہلس دھم

english: Thenceforth AlAkhnas remained ‘the well- rubbed palm tree’ for Bani Zahrah and was blindly obeyed in all relevant matters. Banu Hashim were also inclined to break away, but Abu Jahl’s threats made them desist from that idea.
kashmiri: اتھ پتہٕ بنی زہرا ہٕنٛدس خاطرٕ اوس الاخناز خیرٕ کھجورٕ چ اچھی طرح مسدود تہٕ تمام متعلقہ معاملاتن منٛز اوس اندھس مطٲعنہٕ یوان کرنہٕ۔ بنی ہاشم تہٕ ٲس الگ گژھنٕچ خواہش تھاوان، مگر ابو جہلن ہینز دھمکن کوٚر تمن اتھ خیالس پیٹھ دستخط۔

english: The rest of the army, now 1000 soldiers, approached Badr and encamped themselves beyond a sand dune at Al- ‘Udwat Al- Quswa. ‘The intelligence corps’ of the Madinese army reported to the Prophet ﷺ that a bloody encounter with the Makkans was inescapable, and that a daring step in this context had to be taken, or else the forces of evil would violate the inviolable and would consequently manage to undermine the noble cause of the Islam and tread upon its faithful adherents. The Muslims were afraid that the pagan Makkans would march on and start the war activities within the headquarters of Islam, Madinah.
kashmiri: باقی فوج، یُس اوس 1000 فوجی، بدر کہِ قریب گٲمٕژ تہٕ ال- ودات ال- قوسواہس منز ریتہٕ ہنز ڈائنہٕ پتہٕ کیمپ کرُن۔ مدینی فوج کہِ انٹیلی جنس کورسن کوٚر نبی صلى الله عليه وسلمس اطلاع زِ مکہِن سٕتۍ خونی ملاقات چِھ ناگزیر، تہٕ اتھ تناظرس منز چُھ اکھ جرات مندان قدم ننہٕ یوان، ورنہٕ تہٕ بدچ قوتہٕ چِہ ناقابلِ پامال خلاف ورزی کران تہٕ نتیجس منز چِھ۔ اسلام کہِ شریف مقصدس ہیند نقصان رس

english: A move of such nature would certainly damage and produce an infamous impact on the dignity and stance of the Muslims. On account of the new grave developments, the Prophet ﷺ held an advisory military emergency meeting to review the ongoing situation and exchange viewpoints with the army leaders.
